# Employee Conduct and Disciplinary Policy

## 1. Purpose

This policy describes the standards of behaviour Veltrix expects from everyone who works here, and the fair process the company follows when those standards are not met. Most conduct issues are resolved through a conversation. The formal process exists for the minority of cases where a conversation is not enough, and it is designed so that every employee knows the allegation against them, has a real opportunity to respond, and receives a decision that is proportionate.

## 2. Scope

The policy applies to all employees, interns and fixed-term staff, at work, at company events, on business travel, and online where conduct is connected to the company (for example in TeamTalk channels or on social media when identifying as a Veltrix employee). Contractors are expected to meet the same standards; breaches by contractors are addressed with their supplier under ONB-005.

## 3. Standards of conduct

Every employee is expected to:
- act honestly and never falsify records, timesheets, expense claims, attendance or customer data;
- treat colleagues, candidates, customers and vendors with respect;
- follow company policies, including those on information security (IT-GDL-001), anti-bribery (CMP-001), conflicts of interest and gifts (CMP-002) and the prevention of sexual harassment (CMP-005);
- protect company and customer information;
- be fit for work and not under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs during working hours or at work events where they represent the company;
- attend work as agreed under the Hybrid Work and Attendance Policy (HR-POL-002) and the Leave and Holidays Policy (HR-POL-001);
- raise concerns through proper channels, including the Whistleblower and Speak-Up Policy (CMP-004).

### 3.1 Conduct in specific settings

**Company events and offsites.** The same standards apply at team dinners, offsites and the annual user conference. Where alcohol is served at a company event, employees are expected to drink responsibly; managers present at the event are responsible for ending it if behaviour becomes inappropriate, and the company arranges transport home for late-evening events.

**Online and social media.** Employees may mention that they work at Veltrix on personal profiles, but must make it clear that views are their own, must not share confidential information, and must not post content that harasses or demeans colleagues, customers or competitors. Official company channels are managed only by the Marketing team.

**Customer sites.** When working at a customer's premises, employees follow the customer's site rules in addition to this policy. If the two conflict, the stricter rule applies, and the employee informs their manager.

**Outside work.** Conduct outside work is a matter for this policy only where it has a clear link to the company, for example a criminal conviction relevant to the role, or public behaviour that identifies the employee as a Veltrix representative.

## 4. Misconduct categories

### 4.1 Minor misconduct

Examples: occasional lateness to meetings, repeated failure to mark remote days, careless use of company equipment, unprofessional tone in internal messages. Minor misconduct is normally handled informally by the manager in the first instance.

### 4.2 Serious misconduct

Examples: repeated minor misconduct after a warning, refusing a reasonable instruction, sharing Internal data outside the company, unauthorised absence of three or more consecutive working days, breach of the hybrid policy after a warning, inappropriate comments that fall short of harassment.

### 4.3 Gross misconduct

Gross misconduct is behaviour so serious that it may justify termination for a first offence. Examples include:
- fraud, theft or deliberate falsification of records or expense claims;
- offering or accepting bribes;
- sexual harassment, as determined by the Internal Committee under CMP-005;
- violence or threats of violence;
- deliberate disclosure or theft of Confidential or Restricted data;
- serious breach of information security, such as sharing passwords or disabling security controls deliberately;
- working under the influence of alcohol or drugs in a way that endangers others;
- retaliation against someone who raised a concern in good faith.

## 5. Informal resolution

For minor issues, the manager should speak privately with the employee as soon as possible, explain the concern, listen to the employee's view and agree what needs to change. The manager keeps a brief note of the conversation in PeopleHub under *Manager Notes*. This is not a disciplinary sanction and does not appear in the employee's formal record.

## 6. Formal disciplinary procedure

### 6.1 Investigation

Before any sanction beyond a verbal warning, HR appoints an investigator who has no reporting relationship with the employee or the complainant. The investigator gathers documents, interviews witnesses and the employee, and produces a written report with findings of fact, normally **within 30 days**. Cases involving sexual harassment are investigated by the Internal Committee under CMP-005, and cases involving fraud or bribery may be investigated by the Ethics Committee under CMP-004.

### 6.2 Suspension

Where the allegation is of gross misconduct, or where the employee's presence could hinder the investigation, the CHRO may place the employee on **paid suspension for up to 14 days**, extendable once by 14 days. Suspension is not a sanction and does not imply guilt. During suspension, system access may be restricted by IT on HR's instruction.

### 6.3 Notice of allegation and response

The employee receives a written notice describing the allegation and the evidence. The employee has **3 working days** to respond in writing, and may request a meeting. The employee may be accompanied at the meeting by a colleague of their choice.

### 6.4 Decision and sanctions

| Stage | Typically used for | Decided by |
|---|---|---|
| Verbal warning | First instance of minor misconduct that was not resolved informally | Manager with HR business partner |
| Written warning | Repeated minor misconduct or a first instance of serious misconduct | HR business partner |
| Final written warning | Further misconduct after a written warning, or very serious misconduct | Department head and HR head |
| Termination | Gross misconduct, or further misconduct after a final written warning | CHRO |

Warnings remain **active for 12 months** from the date of issue. An active warning is taken into account if further misconduct occurs. After 12 months the warning remains on file but is not considered in future decisions, except where the same type of serious misconduct recurs.

### 6.5 Appeal

The employee may appeal any formal sanction in writing **within 5 working days** of receiving the decision. The appeal is heard by a manager senior to the person who made the decision, with a different HR representative. The appeal decision is final within the company.

## 7. Absence procedure

When an employee is absent for **3 or more consecutive working days without approval or contact**, the manager and HR follow these steps:
1. Day 3: the manager calls and messages the employee; HR emails the personal email address on file.
2. Day 5: HR sends a written notice to the registered home address asking the employee to report or explain within 3 working days.
3. If there is no response, HR may treat the absence as serious misconduct and start the formal procedure.
Throughout, the company first checks for a genuine emergency, such as a medical crisis.

## 8. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Employee | Meet the standards in section 3; co-operate with investigations; maintain confidentiality |
| Manager | Address issues early and informally; involve HR before any formal step |
| HR business partner | Advise managers; issue written warnings; ensure the process is followed |
| Investigator | Establish facts impartially and report within 30 days |
| Department head and HR head | Decide final written warnings |
| CHRO | Approve suspension and decide terminations |

## 9. Confidentiality and records

Disciplinary records are Restricted data. They are accessible only to HR, the decision-maker and, on appeal, the appeal manager. Witnesses are asked to keep the matter confidential. Records are retained in line with the Data Classification, Handling and Retention Guideline (IT-GDL-004).

## 10. Exceptions

The CHRO may vary the timelines in this policy where an employee is on medical leave, where witnesses are unavailable, or where a criminal investigation is in progress. Any variation is communicated to the employee in writing. The principles of fair notice and a chance to respond are never waived.

## 11. Worked examples

**Example 1 - informal resolution.** Kiran has missed marking remote days in PeopleHub three times in a month. His manager discusses it with him and notes the conversation. No formal warning is issued.

**Example 2 - written warning.** Two months after a verbal warning for repeated lateness to client calls, Tanvi misses another client call without notice. The HR business partner issues a written warning, active for 12 months.

**Example 3 - expense fraud.** An audit finds that an employee submitted the same hotel receipt twice. After investigation confirms the duplication was deliberate, it is treated as gross misconduct, and the CHRO decides on termination.

**Example 4 - appeal.** Rajesh receives a final written warning on Monday. He must submit any appeal by the following Monday (5 working days).

## 12. Frequently asked questions

**Q: How long does a warning stay active?**
A: 12 months from the date it is issued.

**Q: How long do I have to respond to an allegation?**
A: 3 working days from receiving the written notice.

**Q: Can I bring someone to a disciplinary meeting?**
A: Yes, a colleague of your choice.

**Q: How long do I have to appeal a sanction?**
A: 5 working days from receiving the decision.

**Q: Who decides on termination?**
A: The CHRO.

**Q: Does suspension mean I am guilty?**
A: No. Suspension is paid, temporary and not a sanction.

**Q: What happens if I am absent for 3 days without contacting anyone?**
A: Your manager and HR will try to reach you; if there is no response, the absence may be treated as serious misconduct.

## 13. Related documents and references

- HR-POL-001 Leave and Holidays Policy; HR-POL-002 Hybrid Work and Attendance Policy; HR-POL-003 Performance Management Policy

# Acceptable Use of IT Resources Guideline

## 1. Purpose

Veltrix gives its people laptops, accounts, software, networks and collaboration tools so they can do their jobs well. These resources also hold customer data and company secrets, so how they are used directly affects the company's security and reputation. This guideline explains what is expected when using company IT resources, what is permitted for personal use, what is prohibited, and how monitoring works. It is written in plain language so that every employee can follow it without technical knowledge.

## 2. Scope

The guideline covers every person who uses Veltrix IT resources: employees, interns, contractors and visitors given temporary access. "IT resources" include company laptops and phones, email, TeamTalk, PeopleHub, ExpenseDesk, HelpPoint, BuyRight, LeadLoop, TrackWise, cloud storage, office networks and Wi-Fi, the VPN, printers, and any software licensed by the company. It also covers personal devices when they are used to access company email or chat (section 7).

## 3. Key principles

1. **Business purpose:** IT resources are provided for company work. Limited personal use is allowed as described in section 6.
2. **Least privilege:** use only the access you need for your role, and only for its intended purpose.
3. **Protect information:** handle data according to its classification (IT-GDL-004).
4. **Accountability:** you are responsible for activity carried out with your account and device.
5. **Report quickly:** suspected problems are reported immediately, even if you are not sure.

## 4. Company devices

### 4.1 Issue and refresh

Each employee receives a company laptop on the first day of employment (see ONB-003). Laptops are refreshed every **4 years**, or earlier if repair would cost more than 40% of the price of a replacement. Additional equipment, such as a second monitor, can be requested through HelpPoint and is approved by the reporting manager.

### 4.2 Required protections

Company laptops are set up with full-disk encryption, an endpoint detection and response (EDR) agent, automatic updates and device management. Employees must not disable, uninstall or bypass these protections. Laptops lock automatically after **5 minutes** of inactivity; employees should lock the screen manually (Windows key + L, or Control + Command + Q on a Mac) whenever they step away.

### 4.3 Care of devices

- Do not leave a laptop unattended in a car, café or public place.
- Carry laptops in hand luggage when flying.
- Do not allow family members or friends to use a company device.
- Return all devices on your last working day (see HR exit procedures).

### 4.4 Lost or stolen devices

A lost or stolen device must be reported **within 1 hour** of discovery by raising a **P1 ticket** through the IT hotline. IT will remotely lock and wipe the device. Delay in reporting increases the risk to customer data and is treated as a breach of this guideline. For theft, the employee should also file a police report, which is needed for insurance.

## 5. Software and services

### 5.1 Installing software

Software may be installed only from the **Self-Service Portal** or through a HelpPoint request. Requests for new software are reviewed by IT for licensing, security and compatibility. Browser extensions are treated as software: only extensions on the approved list may be installed.

### 5.2 Cloud services and file sharing

Company files must be stored in the company's approved cloud storage, not on personal cloud accounts. Sharing files externally is allowed only through the approved file-sharing tool with link expiry turned on, and only for data classified Public or, under a signed NDA, Confidential (IT-GDL-004).

### 5.3 Generative AI tools

The internal AI knowledge assistant is the only approved tool for working with Confidential data. **Public AI tools may only be used with Public data.** Details are in the AI Assistant and Generative AI Usage Guideline (IT-GDL-005).

### 5.4 Removable storage

USB storage devices are blocked on company laptops by default. If a business need exists (for example delivering a file to a customer who cannot receive it electronically), the CISO may approve an exception for up to 30 days. Approved devices must be encrypted.

## 6. Reasonable personal use

Light personal use is permitted when it:
- happens mostly during breaks;
- does not interfere with work or consume significant network resources;
- does not involve illegal, offensive or sexually explicit material;
- does not involve running a private business, gambling or cryptocurrency mining;
- does not involve storing large personal files, such as personal photo libraries, on the company laptop.

Personal banking, booking a doctor's appointment or reading the news during lunch are examples of acceptable personal use. Employees should not expect privacy for personal content stored on company devices (see section 9).

## 7. Personal devices (BYOD)

Employees may access **company email and TeamTalk only** from a personal smartphone, through the company-managed mobile apps, with MFA enabled and a device screen lock of at least 6 digits. Company data must not be downloaded or stored outside the managed apps. Personal laptops and tablets must not be used to access company systems. If a personal phone with company apps is lost, the employee must report it within 1 hour so IT can remove company data from the managed apps; personal data on the phone is not affected.

## 8. Prohibited activities

The following are never permitted:
- sharing passwords, MFA codes or security keys with anyone, including IT staff;
- accessing or attempting to access systems or data without authorisation;
- copying Confidential or Restricted data to personal email, personal storage or unmanaged devices;
- disabling security software or using tools to bypass network controls, such as unapproved VPNs or proxies;
- installing pirated or unlicensed software;
- sending harassing, discriminatory or defamatory messages;
- using company resources for political campaigning or for commercial activity unrelated to Veltrix;
- connecting unknown devices (for example a found USB drive) to a company laptop.

Breaches are handled under the Employee Conduct and Disciplinary Policy (HR-POL-005). Deliberate data theft or deliberate disabling of security controls may be gross misconduct.

## 9. Monitoring and privacy

Company systems are monitored to protect security, for example through malware detection, login records and data-loss prevention alerts. Monitoring is carried out by the Security team in line with applicable law. **The content of personal communications is not reviewed except during a security or HR investigation approved jointly by the CISO and the CHRO.** Monitoring data is Restricted and retained according to IT-GDL-004.

## 10. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| All users | Follow this guideline, protect devices and credentials, report incidents promptly |
| Reporting manager | Approve reasonable equipment requests, reinforce the guideline in the team |
| IT Service Desk | Provide devices and software, respond to tickets within the priority targets in IT-GDL-003 |
| Security team | Operate monitoring, approve exceptions where delegated, investigate incidents |
| CIO | Own this guideline and the IT environment |
| CISO | Approve security exceptions, including removable storage |

## 11. Exceptions

Exceptions must be requested through HelpPoint under *Security Exception*, stating the business reason, duration and compensating controls. The CISO decides. Exceptions are time-limited (normally no more than 6 months) and are recorded in the security exception register.

## 12. Worked examples

**Example 1 - laptop left in a cab.** Anil realises at 21:10 that he left his laptop in a taxi at 20:30. He must raise a P1 through the IT hotline before 21:30 (within 1 hour of discovering the loss), and then file a police report.

**Example 2 - customer file on USB.** A government customer requires a dataset on encrypted USB. The project manager requests a removable-storage exception; the CISO approves it for 10 days with an encrypted company USB drive.

**Example 3 - personal laptop.** Sneha's company laptop is being repaired, so she wants to log in to LeadLoop from her personal laptop. This is not allowed. IT provides a loaner laptop.

**Example 4 - browser extension.** Rahul wants a grammar-checking browser extension. Because it is not on the approved list and reads page content, he must request it through HelpPoint for IT review.

## 13. Frequently asked questions

**Q: How quickly must I report a lost laptop?**
A: Within 1 hour, by raising a P1 ticket through the IT hotline.

**Q: Can I use my personal phone for work email?**
A: Yes, through the company-managed mobile apps with MFA and a 6-digit screen lock.

**Q: Can I use my personal laptop for work?**
A: No. Personal laptops and tablets must not be used to access company systems.

**Q: How often are laptops replaced?**
A: Every 4 years, or earlier if repair would cost more than 40% of a replacement.

**Q: Can I use a USB drive?**
A: USB storage is blocked by default; the CISO can approve an exception for up to 30 days.

**Q: Will IT read my personal messages?**
A: Not unless the CISO and CHRO jointly approve an investigation.

**Q: Where can I install software from?**
A: Only from the Self-Service Portal or through a HelpPoint request.

# Identity, Password and Access Management Guideline

## 1. Purpose

Most security breaches start with a stolen or misused identity. This guideline sets the rules for passwords, multi-factor authentication (MFA), how access to systems is requested, granted, changed and removed, and how privileged access is controlled. It also explains how role-based access control (RBAC) works across Veltrix systems, including the internal AI knowledge assistant, so that every person sees the information their role requires and nothing more.

## 2. Scope

The guideline covers all user accounts, administrator accounts and service accounts on Veltrix systems, whether hosted in the company's cloud environment or provided by a software-as-a-service vendor. It applies to employees, contractors and interns, and to system owners who approve access.

## 3. Definitions

- **Identity provider (IdP):** the central system that holds user identities and provides single sign-on (SSO) to company applications.
- **System owner:** the manager accountable for a business application, for example the Finance Controller for the finance system.
- **Role:** a named set of access rights linked to a job function, such as *employee*, *hr*, *finance* or *project_manager*.
- **Privileged access:** administrator or other elevated rights that can change system configuration or access all data.
- **Joiner, mover, leaver:** the three events that change a person's access needs.

## 4. Password and authentication standard

| Control | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Minimum password length | **14 characters** |
| Multi-factor authentication | **Mandatory for all systems**, including email, VPN and every SSO application |
| Account lockout | After **5 failed attempts**; the account unlocks automatically after 15 minutes or through the IT Service Desk |
| Screen lock | Automatic after **5 minutes** of inactivity |
| Password change | **No forced periodic change**; change immediately if compromise is suspected |
| Password storage | Only in the company password manager |
| Reuse | The company password must not be used on any other website or service |

### 4.1 Why length instead of complexity

Long passphrases are both easier to remember and harder to crack than short complex passwords. A passphrase of four or more unrelated words, such as "copper lantern monsoon violin", meets the standard. The IdP checks new passwords against lists of known breached passwords and rejects them.

### 4.2 Why no routine rotation

Forcing regular password changes tends to produce predictable patterns (for example adding a number each quarter). Veltrix therefore does not require routine changes. Instead, the IdP monitors for unusual sign-ins, and users must change their password immediately if they suspect it has been exposed.

### 4.3 MFA methods

The approved MFA methods are the company authenticator app with number matching, and hardware security keys. SMS codes are not accepted except as a temporary fallback for up to 7 days while a replacement phone is set up. Never approve an MFA prompt you did not start; report it as a suspected incident (IT-GDL-003).

## 5. Requesting access

### 5.1 Default access

New employees receive default access on their first day: email, TeamTalk, PeopleHub, ExpenseDesk, HelpPoint and the internal AI knowledge assistant (with access matching their role). The provisioning steps are described in ONB-003.

### 5.2 Additional access

1. Raise a request in **HelpPoint > Request Access**, naming the system and the access level needed.
2. The **reporting manager approves first**, confirming the business need.
3. The **system owner approves second**, confirming the access level is appropriate.
4. Access to systems or data classified **Restricted** also requires **Security team approval**.
5. IT grants the access and records it against the person's identity.

Requests that do not state a business reason are returned. Access is always granted to a named individual; **shared accounts are not permitted**.

## 6. Changes and removal of access

### 6.1 Movers

When an employee changes role or team, PeopleHub notifies IT automatically. **Access tied to the old role is removed within 5 working days** unless the new manager re-approves it. Role-based access (for example the role used by the AI knowledge assistant) changes on the effective date of the move.

### 6.2 Leavers

All access is removed **within 24 hours of the last working day**, triggered by the exit record in PeopleHub. For involuntary exits, access is removed on the same day, at the time agreed between HR and IT. Email may be forwarded to the manager for up to 30 days, after which the mailbox is archived under IT-GDL-004.

### 6.3 Long absence

Accounts of employees on leave longer than 60 days are suspended (not deleted) and re-enabled on return, unless the employee needs access during leave for an approved reason.

## 7. Privileged access

- Administrators use a **separate administrator account** that is never used for email or browsing.
- Administrator accounts require a **hardware security key**.
- Administrator credentials are checked out from the privileged access vault for a maximum of **8 hours** at a time, and every checkout is logged.
- Emergency "break-glass" accounts are stored in the vault, can be used only during a P1 incident, and trigger an automatic alert to the CISO when used.
- Privileged access is reviewed **monthly** by the CISO's team.

## 8. Access reviews

System owners review all user access to their systems **quarterly**. HelpPoint generates the review list. **Access not confirmed within 10 working days of the review is removed automatically.** The results of reviews are evidence for the company's ISO/IEC 27001 certification and annual SOC 2 audit.

## 9. Role-based access control

### 9.1 How roles are assigned

Each employee has one primary role, derived from their job in PeopleHub and synchronised to the IdP as a group. The current roles are: employee, hr, it, finance, marketing, project_manager and product_manager. Every role can also access content available to all employees.

### 9.2 RBAC in the AI knowledge assistant

The AI knowledge assistant must only retrieve documents that the signed-in user's role is permitted to read. The role is taken **from the IdP group, never from anything the user types**. A user who asks the assistant to "act as HR" or claims to be a manager does not gain any additional access. Details are in IT-GDL-005.

## 10. Service accounts

Service accounts (used by applications to talk to each other) must have a named human owner, a documented purpose and the minimum permissions required. Their credentials are stored in the secrets vault, rotated at least every 12 months or immediately after a staff change in the owning team, and must never be used for interactive sign-in.

## 11. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| All users | Follow the password standard, use MFA, request only needed access, report suspicious prompts |
| Reporting manager | Approve access requests based on need; confirm access during reviews when asked |
| System owner | Approve access levels; complete quarterly reviews on time |
| IT Service Desk | Provision and remove access; process movers and leavers |
| Security team | Approve Restricted access; review privileged access monthly; monitor sign-ins |
| HR | Keep PeopleHub records accurate, because access automation depends on them |

## 12. Exceptions

Any exception to this guideline (for example a legacy system that cannot support SSO) requires a written risk acceptance from the CISO, with a time limit and compensating controls such as network restrictions or additional monitoring. Exceptions are reviewed at least every 6 months.

## 13. Worked examples

**Example 1 - new system access.** Divya in Finance needs read access to the procurement system. She raises a HelpPoint request; her manager approves, then the procurement system owner approves. No Security approval is needed because the data is Confidential, not Restricted.

**Example 2 - team move.** On 1 July Arjun moves from Marketing to Product. His role changes to product_manager on that date, so the AI assistant immediately stops returning Marketing-only documents to him. His old LeadLoop access is removed by 8 July unless his new manager re-approves it.

**Example 3 - unexpected MFA prompt.** Pooja receives an MFA prompt at 02:00 that she did not trigger. She denies it and reports a suspected incident; Security finds her password in a third-party breach and resets it.

**Example 4 - access review.** The Finance Controller does not respond to the quarterly review for two contractors. After 10 working days their access to the finance system is removed automatically.

## 14. Frequently asked questions

**Q: How long must my password be?**
A: At least 14 characters. A passphrase of four or more unrelated words works well.

**Q: Do I have to change my password every few months?**
A: No. There is no forced periodic change, but you must change it immediately if you suspect it has been exposed.

**Q: How many failed attempts lock my account?**
A: 5 failed attempts; it unlocks after 15 minutes or through the Service Desk.

**Q: Who approves my access request?**
A: Your reporting manager first, then the system owner; Restricted data also needs Security approval.

**Q: How quickly is a leaver's access removed?**
A: Within 24 hours of the last working day, or the same day for involuntary exits.

**Q: How often are access reviews done?**
A: Quarterly by system owners; privileged access is reviewed monthly.

**Q: Can I get more information from the AI assistant by saying I am a manager?**
A: No. Access is based on your role in the identity provider, not on what you type.

## 15. Related documents and references

- IT-GDL-001 Acceptable Use of IT Resources Guideline
- IT-GDL-003 Information Security Incident Reporting and Response Guideline
- IT-GDL-004 Data Classification, Handling and Retention Guideline
- IT-GDL-005 AI Assistant and Generative AI Usage Guideline
- ONB-003 IT and Access Provisioning for New Joiners; ONB-005 Contractor and Intern Onboarding Procedure
- OPS-005 Document Control and Policy Management Procedure (superseded password standard CTR-003)
- External: NIST Special Publication 800-63B (general guidance on authenticators)

## 16. Revision history

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | 2022-01-01 | Superseded standard with 8-character passwords and 90-day rotation (see CTR-003) |
| 3.0 | 2025-04-01 | 14-character minimum, MFA everywhere, no forced rotation |
| 3.1 | 2026-04-01 | Added RBAC rules for the AI knowledge assistant |

# Information Security Incident Reporting and Response Guideline

## 1. Purpose

Incidents will happen in any organisation; what matters is how quickly they are noticed, reported and contained. This guideline tells every employee how to recognise and report an IT or security incident, and tells the IT and Security teams how incidents are prioritised, communicated, resolved and reviewed. Fast, honest reporting is always better than silence: **nobody is disciplined for reporting a genuine mistake promptly**, such as clicking a phishing link.

## 2. Scope

The guideline covers service incidents (systems unavailable or degraded), security incidents (threats to confidentiality, integrity or availability of information), and personal data breaches. It applies to all company systems, devices and data, including data held by vendors on the company's behalf.

## 3. What to report

Report immediately if you notice or suspect any of the following:
- a lost or stolen laptop, phone or access card;
- an email that asks for your password, payment, or urgent action and looks unusual (phishing);
- an MFA prompt you did not start;
- files that have been encrypted or renamed unexpectedly, or a ransom message;
- data sent to the wrong recipient, including emails with attachments;
- a system that is down, very slow, or behaving strangely;
- someone using another person's account or badge;
- a vendor telling you they have had a breach that may involve Veltrix data.

If you are unsure whether something is an incident, report it anyway.

## 4. How to report

| Situation | Channel |
|---|---|
| Suspected security incident, lost device, outage affecting many people | **IT hotline** (staffed 24x7) - this creates a P1 or P2 ticket |
| Phishing email | Use the **Report Phishing** button in the email client; do not forward the email |
| Other IT problems and requests | **HelpPoint** portal |
| Personal data breach | IT hotline **and** inform the Data Protection Officer (see CMP-003) |

When reporting, give your name, the system or device affected, what you saw, when it started, and what you have already done. Do not try to investigate a security incident yourself, do not delete suspicious emails or files, and do not power off an infected laptop - disconnect it from the network instead (turn off Wi-Fi) and wait for instructions.

## 5. Priority levels for IT incidents

| Priority | Definition | First response | Resolution target |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Company-wide outage or security breach | **15 minutes** | **4 hours** |
| P2 | A department or critical system degraded | **1 hour** | **8 hours** |
| P3 | A single user blocked | **4 hours** | **3 business days** |
| P4 | A request or minor issue | **1 business day** | **10 business days** |

The Service Desk sets the priority based on impact and urgency, not on who reports the issue. A reporter can ask for re-prioritisation if the impact is greater than first understood. The company target is that **95% of incidents** are resolved within their resolution target each quarter.

## 6. Security incident severity

Security incidents are additionally given a severity by the Security team.

| Severity | Example | Who is notified | Deadline |
|---|---|---|---|
| SEV-1 | Confirmed breach of customer or Restricted data; ransomware | CISO, CIO, CEO and Legal | **Within 1 hour** of confirmation |
| SEV-2 | One compromised user account; malware on a single device | CISO | **Within 4 hours** |
| SEV-3 | Phishing reported but not clicked; minor policy violation | Security team queue | Next business day |

### 6.1 External reporting

Where an incident is reportable under the CERT-In directions, the Security team notifies CERT-In **within 6 hours** of detection. Notification to customers, regulators and affected individuals is decided by Legal and, for personal data, by the Data Protection Officer under CMP-003. Employees must never contact customers, regulators or the media about an incident themselves.

## 7. Response process

1. **Log and triage.** Every incident is logged in HelpPoint. For P1, the on-call engineer and IT Operations Manager are paged immediately.
2. **Communicate.** For P1 incidents, updates are posted in the TeamTalk incident channel **every 30 minutes**; for P2, **every 2 hours**. Updates say what is known, what is being done, and when the next update will come.
3. **Contain.** Isolate affected devices, disable compromised accounts, block malicious senders or addresses, and preserve evidence.
4. **Eradicate and recover.** Remove the cause, restore from clean backups where needed, and confirm normal service with affected users.
5. **Close.** The ticket is closed only after the reporter or service owner confirms resolution.
6. **Review.** P1 and P2 incidents require a **post-incident review within 5 working days**. SEV-1 and SEV-2 security incidents also require a lessons-learned review **within 10 working days**.

### 7.1 Out-of-hours incidents

Outside business hours (before 08:00 or after 20:00 IST, weekends and holidays), the IT hotline routes calls to the on-call engineer. P1 and P2 incidents are handled immediately with the same targets as during the day. P3 and P4 tickets raised out of hours are picked up at the start of the next business day, and their response clock starts then.

### 7.2 Ransomware and malware

If a laptop shows a ransom message or files are being encrypted, the user must disconnect from the network at once, leave the device powered on, and call the IT hotline. Security isolates the device through the EDR console, checks file shares for spread, and blocks related indicators across the company. Ransom payments are never made without a decision by the CEO on the advice of the CISO and Legal; the company's position is that it does not pay ransoms.

### 7.3 Customer-facing incidents

When an incident affects Veltrix Insight, Veltrix Flow or Veltrix Connect for customers, the status page is updated within 30 minutes of a P1 being declared, and Customer Success informs affected key accounts. Wording for customer communication is approved by the incident lead and, for security incidents, by Legal. A written incident summary is offered to affected customers within 5 working days of resolution.

## 8. Post-incident review

The review is blameless: its aim is to improve systems, not to find someone to punish. It records the timeline, impact, root cause, what went well, what could be improved, and preventive actions with owners and dates. Preventive actions are tracked in HelpPoint until complete. Where a review finds deliberate policy violation, the matter is referred to HR under HR-POL-005 separately from the review.

## 9. Evidence handling

Logs, disk images and relevant emails are preserved before any device is wiped. The Security team maintains chain-of-custody records for evidence that may be needed in legal proceedings. Evidence is classified Restricted and retained according to IT-GDL-004.

## 10. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| All employees | Report incidents immediately; follow instructions; preserve evidence; keep incident details confidential |
| IT Service Desk | Log, prioritise and route incidents; communicate with reporters |
| On-call engineer | Respond to P1 and P2 incidents out of hours |
| IT Operations Manager | Lead P1 incident response; chair post-incident reviews |
| Security team | Investigate security incidents; set severity; handle evidence |
| CISO | Lead SEV-1 and SEV-2 incidents; decide on CERT-In notification |
| Data Protection Officer | Assess personal data breaches and notification duties (CMP-003) |
| Legal | Decide on customer and regulator communication |

## 11. Exceptions

There are no exceptions to the duty to report. Response timelines may be varied by the CISO during a major crisis declared under the Business Continuity and Crisis Management Procedure (OPS-003), in which case the crisis management team sets communication intervals.

## 12. Worked examples

**Example 1 - phishing click.** Harsha clicks a link in an email that looked like a parcel notification and enters her password. She realises the mistake ten minutes later and calls the IT hotline. Security disables her sessions, resets her password and classifies the event as SEV-2. Because she reported promptly, no disciplinary action follows.

**Example 2 - outage.** The VPN fails at 09:20, affecting about 300 remote users. The Service Desk logs a P1. First response must happen by 09:35 and resolution is targeted by 13:20. Updates are posted every 30 minutes.

**Example 3 - wrong recipient.** Manish emails a spreadsheet of customer contact details to the wrong external address. This is a potential personal data breach: he calls the IT hotline and informs the Data Protection Officer, and does not contact the recipient himself.

**Example 4 - single user.** Lata cannot open ExpenseDesk but colleagues can. This is a P3: first response within 4 hours, resolution within 3 business days.

## 13. Frequently asked questions

**Q: Will I get into trouble for reporting that I clicked a phishing link?**
A: No. Prompt reporting of genuine mistakes is never disciplined.

**Q: What is the response time for a P1 incident?**
A: First response within 15 minutes and resolution targeted within 4 hours.

**Q: What should I do with a suspicious email?**
A: Use the Report Phishing button; do not forward or delete it.

**Q: Should I switch off an infected laptop?**
A: No. Disconnect it from the network and wait for instructions.

**Q: How soon must CERT-In be notified of a reportable incident?**
A: Within 6 hours of detection, by the Security team.

**Q: When is a post-incident review required?**
A: For every P1 and P2 incident, within 5 working days.

**Q: How often are updates posted during a P1?**
A: Every 30 minutes in the TeamTalk incident channel.

## 14. Related documents and references

- IT-GDL-001 Acceptable Use of IT Resources Guideline
- IT-GDL-002 Identity, Password and Access Management Guideline
- IT-GDL-004 Data Classification, Handling and Retention Guideline
- CMP-003 Data Protection and Privacy Policy
- OPS-003 Business Continuity and Crisis Management Procedure
- HR-POL-005 Employee Conduct and Disciplinary Policy
- External: CERT-In directions on cyber incident reporting (2022)

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | 2024-04-01 | Combined service and security incident guidance |
| 2.4 | 2026-04-01 | Added personal data breach reporting and blameless review principle |

# Data Classification, Handling and Retention Guideline

## 1. Purpose

Not all information needs the same protection. A published blog post can be shared with anyone, while salary data or a customer's database must be tightly controlled. This guideline gives every employee a simple four-level scheme for classifying information, explains how each level must be stored, shared and destroyed, and sets out how long common types of records are kept. Applying it consistently protects customers and colleagues, keeps Veltrix compliant, and makes systems such as the AI knowledge assistant safer, because access rules depend on correct labels.

## 2. Scope

The guideline covers information in every form: documents, spreadsheets, emails, chat messages, database records, source code, recordings, printed paper and information held by vendors on Veltrix's behalf.

## 3. The four classification levels

| Level | Meaning | Typical examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Public** | Approved for release to anyone | Website content, published blog posts, press releases, public job adverts |
| **Internal** | For use inside the company; low harm if leaked | Most policies, the org chart, internal announcements, holiday calendar |
| **Confidential** | Could harm customers or the company if leaked; shared on a need-to-know basis | Customer data, financial reports, project plans, contracts, product roadmaps, source code |
| **Restricted** | Severe harm if leaked; named individuals only | Salary and bank details, passwords and keys, investigation files, board papers, identity documents, health information |

When in doubt, choose the higher level and ask the information owner.

### 3.1 Who classifies

The person who creates or receives information is responsible for classifying it. The information owner (usually the head of the function that holds it) may reclassify it. Information is Internal by default unless marked otherwise.

### 3.2 Labels in the document library

Documents in the company policy library and the AI knowledge assistant carry a sensitivity label in their metadata. The labels map to the classification levels as follows:

| Metadata label | Classification level | Access |
|---|---|---|
| internal | Internal | All roles |
| restricted | Confidential | Owner role plus named other roles |
| confidential | Restricted | Owner role only |

The metadata labels are used by the access-control system; the classification levels are used in day-to-day language. Both refer to the same scheme.

## 4. Handling rules

| Action | Public | Internal | Confidential | Restricted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Store | Anywhere | Company systems | Company systems with access controls | Approved systems only; access logged |
| Share internally | Freely | Freely | Need to know | Named individuals approved by the owner |
| Share externally | Freely | Not without owner approval | Only under a signed NDA, via approved file sharing | Only with CISO and owner approval, encrypted |
| Email | Allowed | Internal recipients | Internal or NDA recipients; check addresses twice | Encrypted email or secure link only |
| Print | Allowed | Allowed | Collect immediately; no printing at home | Avoid; if essential, collect immediately and shred after use |
| Personal devices | Allowed | Only via managed apps | Not allowed | Not allowed |
| Public AI tools | Allowed | Not allowed | Not allowed | Not allowed |
| Disposal | Normal | Normal deletion | Secure deletion; paper in shredding bins | Secure deletion with record; paper shredded |

Note that only Public data may be entered into public AI tools; this rule is repeated in IT-GDL-001 and IT-GDL-005.

### 4.1 Quick reference for common items

| Item | Classification | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| This guideline and most company policies | Internal | Useful only inside the company; low harm if leaked |
| Team meeting notes | Internal | Unless they discuss customers, finances or people issues |
| A customer's support ticket with user names | Confidential | Contains customer and personal data |
| Monthly management P&L | Confidential | Financial information not yet public |
| Signed customer contract | Confidential | Commercial terms |
| Employee salary or bank details | Restricted | Sensitive personal and financial data |
| HR investigation report | Restricted | Highly sensitive personal information |
| Production database credentials | Restricted | Gives access to customer data |
| Approved press release after publication | Public | Already released |

Classification can change over time. A press release is Internal while in draft and becomes Public only when it is published; financial results become Public only after the company announces them.

## 5. Personal data

Personal data about employees, candidates and customers' users is at least Confidential. Sensitive personal data such as health information, bank details, identity numbers and biometric data is Restricted. Collecting, using and sharing personal data must also follow the Data Protection and Privacy Policy (CMP-003), which requires a lawful purpose and limits use to that purpose.

## 6. Retention schedule

Information must be kept for as long as it is needed for its purpose or required by law, and then securely deleted. The table below sets standard periods. Where a law requires a longer period, the law prevails.

| Record type | Retention period | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Accounting records, invoices, vouchers | **8 years** after the end of the financial year | Finance |
| Employee personnel file, including disciplinary records | **7 years** after the employee leaves | HR |
| Payroll records | 8 years after the end of the financial year | Finance (Payroll) |
| Background verification reports | **2 years** after the employee leaves | HR |
| Unsuccessful candidate data | **12 months** after the hiring decision (HR-POL-004) | HR |
| Customer data in production systems | Deleted **within 90 days** of contract end, unless the contract says otherwise | Product / Engineering |
| Contracts | 8 years after expiry | Legal |
| Mailboxes of leavers | Archived for **3 years**, then deleted | IT |
| System and security logs | **1 year** | IT / Security |
| AI knowledge assistant conversation logs | **90 days** (IT-GDL-005) | IT |
| Backups | **35 days**; monthly copies kept for 12 months | IT |
| CCTV footage | **30 days** (OPS-004) | Facilities |
| Visitor logs | 1 year | Facilities |
| Superseded policies | 7 years after supersession, marked as superseded (OPS-005) | Policy owner |

### 6.1 Legal hold

When Legal issues a legal hold (for example because of a dispute or investigation), the affected records must not be deleted even if their retention period has ended. The hold overrides this schedule until Legal lifts it in writing.

### 6.2 Deletion

Deletion must be secure: electronic records are deleted using the system's standard deletion, with cloud storage set to permanently purge after the retention period; devices are wiped to the NIST 800-88 standard before reuse or disposal; paper is placed in locked shredding bins. Deletion of Restricted records is recorded in a deletion log.

## 7. Data owners and custodians

- **Information owner:** decides the classification, approves access and external sharing, and confirms retention.
- **Custodian (usually IT):** operates the systems that store the information and applies the technical controls.
- **User:** handles the information according to its classification.

## 8. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| All employees | Classify what they create; handle information according to the rules in section 4 |
| Information owners | Approve access and external sharing; review classification annually |
| IT | Provide storage, encryption, backup and deletion capabilities; apply labels in systems |
| Security team | Monitor for data leakage; approve Restricted external sharing with the owner |
| Legal | Issue and lift legal holds; advise on statutory retention |
| Data Protection Officer | Oversee personal data handling under CMP-003 |

## 9. Exceptions

Exceptions to handling rules (for example sending Restricted data to a regulator through a channel they require) must be approved in advance by the CISO and the information owner and recorded in the security exception register.

## 10. Worked examples

**Example 1 - roadmap to a partner.** A product manager wants to send the product roadmap (Confidential) to an implementation partner. This is allowed only if a signed NDA is in place, and only through the approved file-sharing tool with link expiry.

**Example 2 - salary sheet.** An HR analyst needs to send a salary file (Restricted) to the payroll vendor. This requires owner and CISO approval and an encrypted channel; the analyst must not attach it to a normal email.

**Example 3 - candidate CV from last year.** A recruiter finds CVs of unsuccessful candidates from 14 months ago in a shared folder. These have passed the 12-month retention period and must be deleted unless the candidates agreed to longer retention.

**Example 4 - public AI tool.** A marketer wants to paste a draft press release (not yet published, so Internal) into a public AI tool to improve the wording. This is not allowed; only Public data may be used. The internal AI assistant can be used instead.

## 11. Frequently asked questions

**Q: What are the four classification levels?**
A: Public, Internal, Confidential and Restricted.

**Q: Is customer data Confidential or Restricted?**
A: Customer data is at least Confidential; sensitive items such as identity numbers or health data are Restricted.

**Q: How long are accounting records kept?**
A: 8 years after the end of the financial year.

**Q: How long are employee records kept after someone leaves?**
A: 7 years, except background verification reports, which are kept for 2 years.

**Q: How long are AI assistant conversation logs kept?**
A: 90 days.

**Q: What happens to records under legal hold?**
A: They must not be deleted until Legal lifts the hold, even if the retention period has ended.

**Q: What does the "restricted" label in document metadata mean?**
A: It corresponds to the Confidential level: the owner role and named other roles can access it.

## 12. Related documents and references

- IT-GDL-001 Acceptable Use of IT Resources Guideline; IT-GDL-002 Identity, Password and Access Management Guideline; IT-GDL-003 Incident Reporting and Response; IT-GDL-005 AI Assistant and Generative AI Usage Guideline
- CMP-003 Data Protection and Privacy Policy
- HR-POL-004 Recruitment and Selection Policy
- OPS-004 Facilities, Office Access and Workplace Safety Procedure
- OPS-005 Document Control and Policy Management Procedure
- External: Companies Act, 2013 (books of account); Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023

## 13. Revision history

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.3 | 2024-04-01 | Four-level classification introduced |
| 2.0 | 2026-04-01 | Retention schedule merged into this guideline; metadata label mapping added |

applies_to: All employees and contractors who use the internal AI knowledge assistant or any generative AI tool for work
source_reference: Fictional academic sample guideline for Veltrix Systems Pvt. Ltd.
full_text:
# AI Assistant and Generative AI Usage Guideline

## 1. Purpose

Veltrix provides an internal AI knowledge assistant that answers questions using company documents, explains business rules, guides people through workflows and supports decisions with evidence. Generative AI can save a great deal of time, but it can also be wrong, it can expose data if used carelessly, and it can be manipulated. This guideline explains how the assistant works, what it may and may not be used for, how its access controls protect information, and how employees should use public generative AI tools.

## 2. Scope

The guideline applies to the internal AI knowledge assistant and to any external generative AI service (chatbots, writing assistants, code assistants, image generators) used for Veltrix work, on any device.

## 3. How the internal assistant works

The assistant uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). When you ask a question:
1. The assistant identifies your **role from the identity provider** (IT-GDL-002).
2. It searches the company document library, **only among documents your role is permitted to read**.
3. It passes the most relevant passages to a language model, which writes an answer based on those passages.
4. It shows the **source documents and sections** it used, so you can check the answer.

Because access is filtered before retrieval, the assistant cannot use a document you are not allowed to see, even if your question mentions it. If the answer requires such a document, the assistant replies that it cannot share that information with your role and suggests contacting the owning team. It will not reveal the title or content of documents outside your access.

## 4. Approved uses

The assistant may be used to:
- find and explain company policies, procedures and rules;
- guide you step by step through a workflow, such as submitting an expense claim or requesting access;
- summarise long documents you have access to;
- compare options against a framework (for example the approval levels in the Delegation of Authority, OPS-002);
- draft internal emails, documents and meeting notes;
- answer questions about Confidential data that your role can access.

## 5. Decision support, not decision making

The assistant **supports decisions; it does not approve spend, hires, terminations, access requests or changes**. Approvals always follow the Delegation of Authority (OPS-002) and the relevant policy, and must be made by the accountable person in the proper system (for example BuyRight for purchases or PeopleHub for leave).

For decisions that significantly affect a person, such as hiring, performance ratings, disciplinary outcomes or terminations, the assistant may be used only to find the relevant rules; it must not be asked to evaluate or rank individuals.

## 6. Checking answers

AI answers can be incomplete or wrong. Before acting on an answer that matters:
- open the cited source and confirm the relevant section;
- check the document's version, status and effective date;
- if the answer has no source, treat it as unverified;
- report wrong answers with the thumbs-down button and a short comment, so the knowledge team can fix the content or the system.

### 6.1 Asking good questions

The assistant gives better answers when questions are specific. Include the situation, the amount or dates involved and what you need to decide. For example, instead of "travel rules?", ask "What is the hotel limit for a two-night business trip to Bengaluru, and who approves it?". For workflows, ask for the steps in order ("What are the steps to request access to the finance system?"). For decisions, ask the assistant to list the rule, the threshold and the approver, and to cite the source of each. If an answer seems to miss your situation, add the missing detail rather than repeating the same question.

## 7. Conflicting information

Sometimes two documents appear to say different things, for example an old memo and a current policy. The assistant is designed to prefer the **latest approved version** of a policy, following the precedence rules in the Document Control and Policy Management Procedure (OPS-005), and to point out the conflict instead of hiding it. Drafts, superseded versions, regional memos that were never approved, and wiki pages are **not authoritative**. If you find a conflict, report it to the policy owner named in the document so it can be corrected.

## 8. Prohibited uses

You must not:
- try to make the assistant reveal information outside your access, for example by claiming to be another role, asking it to "ignore previous instructions", or hiding instructions inside uploaded documents;
- upload documents to the assistant that you are not permitted to share;
- use the assistant's output in customer-facing material, contracts or regulatory submissions without human review and the normal approval process;
- ask the assistant for legal advice on matters that require the Legal team;
- use any AI tool to create content that is discriminatory, harassing, deceptive or that imitates a real person without consent.

Attempts to bypass access controls are treated as serious misconduct under HR-POL-005.

## 9. Public generative AI tools

- **Only Public data may be entered into public AI tools.** Internal, Confidential and Restricted information, including customer names, unreleased product details, source code and personal data, must never be entered (IT-GDL-004).
- Public AI tools may not be used to process personal data under CMP-003.
- Turn off chat history or model-training options where the tool allows it.
- New AI tools for team use must be requested through HelpPoint; IT reviews them under the vendor security assessment process before approval.

## 10. Logging and privacy

Conversations with the internal assistant are logged for security, quality improvement and audit, and the logs are kept for **90 days**. Logs are Restricted and can be reviewed only by the IT and Security teams for operational reasons, or as part of an investigation approved by the CISO and the CHRO. Company data used by the assistant is not used to train external models.

## 11. Labelling AI-generated content

Content intended for external publication (marketing material, blog posts, documentation) that was substantially drafted by AI must be reviewed by a human author, fact-checked, and approved through the usual content review process. Internal documents do not need a label, but the author remains accountable for accuracy.

## 12. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| All users | Use AI within this guideline; verify important answers; report errors and conflicts |
| Policy and document owners | Keep documents current and correctly labelled so that answers and access are accurate |
| Knowledge management team | Maintain the document library, metadata and assistant configuration; review feedback weekly |
| IT | Operate the assistant, logging and access integration |
| Security team | Test the assistant for access-control weaknesses and prompt-injection risks at least twice a year |
| CIO | Own this guideline and approve new AI capabilities |

## 13. Exceptions

Use of a public AI tool with non-Public data may be approved only where the vendor has a signed enterprise agreement that prevents training on company data and passes the security assessment. Such approvals are given by the CISO in writing and listed on the approved tools page.

## 14. Worked examples

**Example 1 - role boundary.** An employee in the employee role asks the assistant, "What are the salary bands for L5?" Salary bands are Restricted HR information. The assistant replies that it cannot share that information with the employee's role and suggests contacting HR. It does not confirm whether such a document exists.

**Example 2 - workflow assistance.** A project manager asks how to buy a Rs 3,00,000 software subscription. The assistant explains that a purchase order and three quotes are required, that the department head approves at this amount, and cites OPS-001 and OPS-002. The project manager then raises the request in BuyRight.

**Example 3 - conflict found.** A user asks about hotel limits in Pune and the assistant finds both the current Business Travel Policy and an old regional memo with a higher limit. It answers with the approved policy's limit, notes that the memo is unofficial, and cites both.

**Example 4 - public tool misuse.** A developer pastes proprietary source code into a public chatbot to debug it. This breaches the guideline because source code is Confidential. The developer should report it as an incident under IT-GDL-003.

## 15. Frequently asked questions

**Q: Can the assistant show me documents that my role cannot access?**
A: No. It searches only documents permitted for your role, and it will not reveal the title or content of others.

**Q: Can the assistant approve my purchase or leave request?**
A: No. It supports decisions, but approvals must be made by the accountable person in the proper system.

**Q: What should I do if the assistant gives an answer without a source?**
A: Treat it as unverified and check the relevant policy before acting.

**Q: How long are my conversations with the assistant kept?**
A: 90 days.

**Q: Can I use a public AI chatbot to summarise an internal report?**
A: No. Only Public data may be entered into public AI tools.

**Q: What happens when two documents conflict?**
A: The latest approved version prevails under OPS-005; drafts, memos and superseded versions are not authoritative.

## 16. Related documents and references

- IT-GDL-001 Acceptable Use of IT Resources Guideline; IT-GDL-002 Identity, Password and Access Management Guideline; IT-GDL-003 Incident Reporting and Response; IT-GDL-004 Data Classification, Handling and Retention Guideline
- OPS-002 Delegation of Authority and Approval Workflow; OPS-005 Document Control and Policy Management Procedure
- CMP-003 Data Protection and Privacy Policy

## 17. Revision history

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 2025-07-01 | First release with the internal assistant pilot |
| 1.2 | 2026-04-01 | Added conflict handling, decision-support limits and prompt-injection rules |

# New Employee Onboarding Programme (First 90 Days)

## 1. Purpose

The first three months in a new job shape how quickly a person becomes productive and whether they decide to stay. Veltrix's onboarding programme gives every new employee a clear, well-supported path from accepting an offer to working confidently and independently. This document explains what happens before the first day, on the first day, in the first week, and through the first 90 days, and who is responsible for each step. It is the main reference for new joiners; managers have a companion guide (ONB-002), and IT provisioning is described in ONB-003.

## 2. Scope

The programme applies to all new permanent and fixed-term employees in every office and in remote roles. Interns and contractors follow a shorter version described in ONB-005. Employees transferring between offices do not repeat the full programme but complete the location-specific parts in section 6.

## 3. Programme at a glance

| Stage | Timing | Key outcomes |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-boarding | From offer acceptance to joining day | Documents submitted, accounts created, laptop ready, buddy assigned |
| Day 1 | Joining day (always a Monday) | Welcome, laptop handover, MFA set-up, meet manager and buddy |
| Week 1 | First 5 working days | Company induction, systems set-up, first goals discussed |
| Days 1-30 | First month | Mandatory training completed, benefits enrolled, 30-day check-in |
| Days 31-60 | Second month | Role-specific learning, first independent tasks, 60-day check-in |
| Days 61-90 | Third month | Full ownership of core responsibilities, 90-day review |
| Probation end | Month 6 | Confirmation review under ONB-004 |

## 4. Before the first day (pre-boarding)

### 4.1 Joining dates

New employees join on a **Monday**, or on the next working day if Monday is a public holiday. This allows the weekly induction and IT set-up to run efficiently. Exceptions require the HR business partner's approval.

### 4.2 Documents

After accepting the offer, the joiner receives a PeopleHub pre-boarding link and uploads:
- government photo identity proof and PAN;
- address proof;
- educational certificates for the highest qualification;
- relieving or experience letters from previous employers;
- bank account details for salary;
- a passport-size photograph for the ID card.
Documents are personal data and are handled under the Data Protection and Privacy Policy (CMP-003).

### 4.3 Background verification

Background verification starts once the offer is accepted and must be completed **within 30 days of joining**, as described in the Recruitment and Selection Policy. The joiner can start work while it is in progress.

### 4.4 Accounts and laptop

HR confirms the joining date in PeopleHub, which triggers IT provisioning. **Accounts are created 2 working days before the joining date**, and the laptop is prepared so that it is ready on day 1 (ONB-003). Account details are never sent by email; they are handed over in person or by video call on the first day.

### 4.5 Buddy

The manager assigns an **onboarding buddy** at least one week before the joining date. The buddy is an experienced colleague, not the manager, who helps the joiner with practical questions during the first 90 days. The buddy sends a welcome message before day 1.

### 4.6 Relocation

Joiners who are relocating receive support under the Relocation and Joining Expense Policy (FIN-RMB-003), including temporary accommodation for up to 15 nights.

## 5. Day 1

| Time | Activity | With |
|---|---|---|
| 09:30 | Welcome at reception; ID card and access badge | Facilities and HR Operations |
| 10:00 | Laptop handover, MFA enrolment, password manager set-up | IT Service Desk |
| 11:30 | Meet the manager: role overview, team introductions | Manager |
| 13:00 | Lunch with the buddy and team | Buddy |
| 14:30 | PeopleHub walk-through: profile, leave, payslips | HR Operations |
| 16:00 | Wrap-up with the manager: plan for week 1 | Manager |

Remote joiners receive their laptop by courier before day 1 and complete the same steps by video call.

## 6. Week 1

- **Company induction** (half a day): history, values, products (Veltrix Insight, Veltrix Flow, Veltrix Connect), customers, and how the company is organised.
- **Policy essentials**: hybrid work (HR-POL-002), leave (HR-POL-001), conduct (HR-POL-005), acceptable use of IT (IT-GDL-001) and passwords (IT-GDL-002).
- **Location briefing** for the base office: building access, emergency exits and assembly points, first aiders, canteen and transport.
- **Tools**: TeamTalk, email and calendar, TrackWise and any role-specific systems requested by the manager.
- **First goals conversation** with the manager: what success looks like at 30, 60 and 90 days.

## 7. Days 1-30: settling in

### 7.1 Mandatory training

The following must be completed **within 30 days of joining**:
1. Code of Conduct and Ethics;
2. Information Security Awareness;
3. Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) awareness (CMP-005);
4. Data Protection and Privacy (CMP-003);
5. Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption (CMP-001).
PeopleHub tracks completion. Incomplete mandatory training after 30 days is reported to the manager and HR, and system access may be limited until it is done.

### 7.2 Benefits enrolment

Enrol dependants in group health insurance (a **Rs 5,00,000 family floater**) and confirm nominations for life insurance and provident fund in PeopleHub **within 30 days of joining**. After 30 days, dependants can only be added after a life event such as marriage or birth.

### 7.3 30-day check-in

The manager holds a structured check-in covering what is going well, what is confusing, whether the joiner has the access and tools they need, and progress against 30-day goals. The joiner also completes a short new-joiner survey.

## 8. Days 31-60: building capability

- Role-specific learning, using the learning budget (FIN-RMB-004) where useful.
- Shadowing experienced colleagues in customer meetings, releases or close processes, depending on the role.
- First independent tasks with clear review points.
- **60-day check-in** with the manager, focusing on skills, relationships and any support needed.

## 9. Days 61-90: taking ownership

By day 90 the joiner should own the core responsibilities of the role with normal levels of support. The **90-day review** is a written conversation recorded in PeopleHub that confirms goals for the rest of probation, identifies development needs, and gives early feedback on whether the joiner is on track for confirmation. A second new-joiner survey is sent at day 90.

### 9.1 Improving the programme

The 30-day and 90-day new-joiner surveys ask about the clarity of the role, the usefulness of the induction, readiness of tools and access, and support from the manager and buddy. HR Operations reviews the results every quarter with the IT Service Desk and department heads and publishes the main changes made in response. Joiners can also share suggestions at any time through PeopleHub.

## 10. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| New employee | Submit documents on time, complete mandatory training within 30 days, ask questions, give feedback |
| Manager | Plan the first 90 days, assign a buddy, hold 30, 60 and 90-day check-ins (see ONB-002) |
| Buddy | Answer practical questions, introduce people, check in weekly during the first month |
| HR Operations | Run pre-boarding, PeopleHub set-up, induction and benefits enrolment |
| IT Service Desk | Create accounts, prepare and hand over the laptop, enrol MFA (ONB-003) |
| Facilities | Issue ID card and badge, provide a desk and location briefing |
| HR business partner | Monitor progress, help resolve issues, review survey feedback |

## 11. Exceptions

Senior hires at L6 and above follow an extended programme that adds meetings with each member of the leadership team in the first month. Joiners returning to Veltrix within 12 months of leaving complete only mandatory training and the policy updates briefing. Any other variation needs the HR business partner's agreement.

## 12. Worked examples

**Example 1 - accounts.** Neha's joining date is Monday 6 July. IT creates her accounts by Thursday 2 July, two working days before joining, and her laptop is ready on 6 July.

**Example 2 - missed training.** Arjun has not completed the Data Protection module by day 30. HR notifies his manager, and his access to customer data systems is limited until he completes it.

**Example 3 - adding a spouse to insurance.** Farah joins in May and gets married in December. Because marriage is a life event, she can add her spouse to health insurance in December even though the 30-day joining window has passed.

**Example 4 - remote joiner.** Vikas joins a remote role in Kochi. His laptop is couriered to arrive by the Friday before he joins, and IT completes MFA enrolment with him by video call on Monday morning.

## 13. Frequently asked questions

**Q: What day of the week do new employees join?**
A: Monday, or the next working day if Monday is a public holiday.

**Q: When are my accounts created?**
A: Two working days before your joining date; you receive your details on day 1.

**Q: Which training must I complete in the first 30 days?**
A: Code of Conduct, Information Security, POSH awareness, Data Protection and Anti-Bribery.

**Q: When must I enrol dependants in health insurance?**
A: Within 30 days of joining.

**Q: Who is my onboarding buddy?**
A: An experienced colleague assigned by your manager at least one week before you join.

**Q: What check-ins will I have?**
A: At 30, 60 and 90 days, followed by the confirmation review at the end of probation.

**Q: How long is the probation period?**
A: Six months; see ONB-004.

## 14. Related documents and references

- ONB-002 Manager's Onboarding Responsibilities Guide; ONB-003 IT and Access Provisioning for New Joiners; ONB-004 Probation and Confirmation Policy; ONB-005 Contractor and Intern Onboarding Procedure
- HR-POL-001 Leave and Holidays Policy; HR-POL-002 Hybrid Work and Attendance Policy; HR-POL-005 Employee Conduct and Disciplinary Policy
- IT-GDL-001 Acceptable Use of IT Resources Guideline; IT-GDL-002 Identity, Password and Access Management Guideline
- CMP-001 Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy; CMP-003 Data Protection and Privacy Policy; CMP-005 POSH Policy
- FIN-RMB-003 Relocation and Joining Expense Policy; FIN-RMB-004 Learning Reimbursement Policy
- Labelled contradiction example: CTR-005 (unofficial team wiki page)

## 15. Revision history

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | 2025-04-01 | Introduced 30/60/90-day structure and buddy programme |
| 2.3 | 2026-04-01 | Monday joining rule; anti-bribery added to mandatory training |
