full_text:
# Manager's Onboarding Responsibilities Guide

## 1. Purpose

A new employee's manager has more influence on their first months than anyone else. This guide tells managers exactly what to do, and when, so that every new team member gets a consistent, high-quality start. It complements the New Employee Onboarding Programme (ONB-001), which is written for joiners, and links to the probation process (ONB-004). It is restricted to people managers and HR because it includes guidance on assessing and addressing early performance concerns.

## 2. Scope

The guide applies to every manager who receives a new permanent or fixed-term employee, whether hired externally, transferred from another team, or returning from long leave into a new role. Managers of interns and contractors should use the shorter checklist in ONB-005.

## 3. Why it matters

Veltrix tracks two onboarding measures for every department: the **new-joiner survey score** at 30 and 90 days (target **4 out of 5 or higher**) and **early attrition**, meaning joiners who leave within their first 6 months. Departments with early attrition above 10% in a year review their onboarding with their HR business partner. Most early exits are linked to unclear expectations, missing tools or lack of manager time in the first weeks, all of which this guide addresses.

## 4. Manager checklist

### 4.1 As soon as the offer is accepted

- [ ] Confirm the joining date with Talent Acquisition; joining days are Mondays (ONB-001).
- [ ] Send a short personal welcome message.
- [ ] Decide which role-specific systems the joiner will need beyond the default access.
- [ ] Inform the team of the new joiner's name, role and start date.

### 4.2 At least 5 working days before joining

- [ ] Raise **HelpPoint access requests for role-specific systems** (for example LeadLoop, TrackWise projects, finance systems), so that IT can complete approvals before day 1. Default accounts are created automatically 2 working days before joining (ONB-003).
- [ ] Request additional equipment (second monitor, headset) through HelpPoint.
- [ ] Confirm a desk with Facilities if the joiner will be office-based on day 1.

### 4.3 At least 1 week before joining

- [ ] **Assign an onboarding buddy** from the team or a neighbouring team. Choose someone with at least 12 months of service, good knowledge of how things work, and time to help. Do not assign yourself.
- [ ] Prepare a first-week schedule, including introductions to key colleagues outside the team.
- [ ] Draft 30, 60 and 90-day goals.

### 4.4 Day 1

- [ ] Block at least two hours of your own time: a morning meeting and an end-of-day wrap-up.
- [ ] Explain the role, how it connects to team and company goals, and how the team works (meetings, anchor days, tools).
- [ ] Share the first-week schedule.
- [ ] Introduce the buddy and the team.

### 4.5 Week 1

- [ ] Agree the 30, 60 and 90-day goals and record them in PeopleHub.
- [ ] Check that the joiner has all access needed; escalate missing access through HelpPoint.
- [ ] Hold a short daily check-in.

## 5. Setting early goals

Early goals should balance learning and contribution. A useful pattern is:
- **By day 30:** understands the team's work, products and key processes; has completed mandatory training; has delivered one small piece of real work.
- **By day 60:** handles routine tasks independently; has contributed to a larger piece of work with guidance.
- **By day 90:** owns core responsibilities; can explain priorities for the rest of probation.

Goals should be specific to the role. For a product manager, a day-60 goal might be "write and get approval for one feature specification"; for a finance analyst, "prepare the month-end accrual schedule for one cost centre with review".

## 6. Check-ins and reviews

| Check-in | Timing | Focus | Record in PeopleHub? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weekly one-to-one | Throughout probation | Progress, blockers, feedback | Brief notes |
| 30-day check-in | Around day 30 | Settling in, access, early goals | Yes |
| 60-day check-in | Around day 60 | Skills, independence, relationships | Yes |
| 90-day review | Around day 90 | Ownership, goals for rest of probation, early feedback on confirmation | Yes |
| Confirmation review | 2 weeks before probation ends | Recommendation to confirm, extend or end (ONB-004) | Yes |

Manager notes must be factual and professional. Employees can request access to their records, and notes may be relevant evidence in any later decision.

### 6.1 Giving useful feedback to new joiners

New joiners often hesitate to ask for feedback because they do not want to appear unsure. Make feedback a normal part of every one-to-one rather than an event. Good feedback in the first months:
- is **timely**, given within a day or two of the work it relates to;
- is **specific**, describing what was done and its effect ("the summary you wrote for the customer was clear and they approved it without changes");
- separates **learning gaps** (things nobody has explained yet) from **performance gaps** (things the joiner knows but does not do);
- ends with a clear next step.

Ask the joiner for feedback too: what has been confusing, what would have helped them start faster, and whether they have the access and information they need. Share recurring themes with the HR business partner so the onboarding programme can improve.

## 7. Addressing early concerns

If you have concerns about a new employee's performance or conduct:
1. Raise them **early and specifically** in a one-to-one, with examples.
2. Agree what needs to change and what support you will provide.
3. Record the conversation in PeopleHub.
4. Inform your HR business partner.

**Concerns that could lead to an extension or ending of probation must be documented by the end of month 4.** Raising them for the first time at the confirmation review is unfair to the employee and makes it difficult to justify a decision. Probation outcomes are described in ONB-004; the performance review process in HR-POL-003 does not apply until confirmation.

## 8. Remote and hybrid joiners

For remote joiners, confirm with IT that the laptop has been couriered to arrive before day 1 and schedule the day-1 set-up by video. Plan at least one in-person team visit during the first 60 days where practical; travel is booked under the Business Travel Policy. For hybrid joiners, align the joiner's office days with team anchor days during the first month so they can learn from colleagues in person.

## 9. Internal transfers

When an employee joins your team from another team, there is no new-joiner programme, but you should still: agree new goals within 2 weeks, request any new access and confirm that access from the previous role is removed or re-approved (IT-GDL-002), introduce key contacts, and hold a 30-day check-in.

## 10. New managers

Employees who become managers for the first time, whether by promotion or hiring, complete the *Management Essentials* learning path within 90 days of taking on the role. The path covers one-to-ones, goal setting, feedback, performance management, recruitment and the legal basics of managing people. It is funded centrally and does not use the individual learning budget (FIN-RMB-004).

## 11. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Manager | Complete the checklist, set goals, hold check-ins, address concerns early, recommend probation outcome |
| Buddy | Practical support and introductions; weekly check-in during the first month |
| HR business partner | Coach managers, review survey and early-attrition data, advise on concerns |
| IT Service Desk | Provision default and requested access before day 1 |
| Facilities | Desk, ID card and badge on day 1 |

## 12. Exceptions

Where a manager is on leave when a joiner starts, the manager must nominate a deputy manager who completes the day-1 and week-1 steps. Where a new team is being formed and no buddy with 12 months of service is available, the HR business partner may assign a buddy from another department.

## 13. Worked examples

**Example 1 - access before day 1.** A new sales engineer joins on 14 September. The manager raises the LeadLoop access request on 3 September, more than 5 working days earlier, so approvals are complete before day 1.

**Example 2 - late concern.** In month 5, a manager decides to recommend extending a joiner's probation but has no recorded concerns. The HR business partner advises that, because concerns were not documented by month 4, the manager should first hold a documented conversation and support plan before recommending an extension.

**Example 3 - buddy choice.** A manager plans to buddy a new hire with an employee who joined 7 months ago. Because buddies should have at least 12 months of service, the manager chooses a different colleague.

## 14. Frequently asked questions

**Q: When should I request role-specific access for a new joiner?**
A: At least 5 working days before the joining date, through HelpPoint.

**Q: When must I assign a buddy?**
A: At least one week before the joining date.

**Q: Can I be the buddy myself?**
A: No. The buddy must be someone other than the manager.

**Q: By when must probation concerns be documented?**
A: By the end of month 4.

**Q: What is the target new-joiner survey score?**
A: 4 out of 5 or higher.

**Q: What is early attrition?**
A: Joiners who leave within their first 6 months.

**Q: What training do new managers complete?**
A: The Management Essentials learning path, within 90 days of taking on the role.

## 15. Related documents and references

- ONB-001 New Employee Onboarding Programme; ONB-003 IT and Access Provisioning for New Joiners; ONB-004 Probation and Confirmation Policy; ONB-005 Contractor and Intern Onboarding Procedure
- HR-POL-003 Performance Management Policy; HR-POL-004 Recruitment and Selection Policy
- IT-GDL-002 Identity, Password and Access Management Guideline
- FIN-RMB-002 Business Travel Policy; FIN-RMB-004 Learning Reimbursement Policy

## 16. Revision history

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 2025-04-01 | First manager guide |
| 1.5 | 2026-04-01 | Added month-4 documentation rule and new-manager learning path |

# IT and Access Provisioning for New Joiners

## 1. Purpose

A new joiner who spends the first days waiting for a laptop or a password loses momentum and forms a poor first impression. A joiner who receives too much access creates a security risk. This procedure explains how IT, HR and hiring managers work together so that every new employee has the right equipment and the right access on their first day, and no more access than their role needs.

## 2. Scope

The procedure covers laptops and peripherals, default accounts, role-specific access, multi-factor authentication, and access to the internal AI knowledge assistant for new permanent and fixed-term employees. Contractors and interns follow the same steps with the differences described in ONB-005.

## 3. How provisioning is triggered

Provisioning is automated from PeopleHub. When HR Operations marks a candidate as *Joining confirmed* and enters the joining date, base office, department, grade, job title and reporting manager, PeopleHub creates an onboarding ticket in HelpPoint. **Accurate PeopleHub data is essential**: the department and job title determine the joiner's role in the identity provider, and therefore what the AI knowledge assistant and other role-based systems will show them.

## 4. Timeline

| When | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Joining confirmed (normally at least 10 working days before joining) | Onboarding ticket created; laptop allocated from stock | HR Operations, IT |
| 5 working days before joining | Manager raises role-specific access requests | Hiring manager |
| **2 working days before joining** | **Default accounts created**; laptop imaged, encrypted and enrolled | IT Service Desk |
| 1 working day before joining | Final check: laptop, accounts, requested access approved | IT Service Desk |
| Day 1 | Laptop handover, MFA enrolment, password manager set-up | IT Service Desk and joiner |
| Week 1 | Remaining access requests completed | IT, system owners |

For remote joiners, the laptop is couriered so that it **arrives by the Friday before the joining date**, and the day-1 set-up is done by video call.

## 5. Equipment

### 5.1 Standard laptop

Every employee receives a company laptop. The standard configuration has at least 16 GB of memory and a 512 GB encrypted solid-state drive. Engineering and data roles receive a higher-specification model with 32 GB of memory. All laptops are enrolled in device management and run the EDR agent before handover. Laptops are refreshed every 4 years (IT-GDL-001).

### 5.2 Peripherals

A headset is provided to everyone. Monitors, docking stations, keyboards and mice are available at office desks; employees with approved fully remote arrangements may request a monitor for home through HelpPoint with manager approval.

## 6. Accounts and default access

On day 1, every new employee has:
- a company email account and calendar;
- TeamTalk (chat and video);
- PeopleHub (HR self-service);
- ExpenseDesk (expenses and travel);
- HelpPoint (IT support and requests);
- the internal AI knowledge assistant, with access matching the joiner's role;
- the company password manager.

Account names follow the format firstname.lastname, with a number added where a duplicate exists. **Credentials are never sent by email**; the temporary password is handed over in person or by video call on day 1 and must be changed at first sign-in to a passphrase of at least **14 characters** (IT-GDL-002).

## 7. Multi-factor authentication

MFA is mandatory for all systems. On day 1 the IT Service Desk helps the joiner install the company authenticator app on their phone and register a backup method. Engineering, IT and Finance staff who will hold privileged or payment-related access also receive a hardware security key in their first week. Joiners without a suitable smartphone are issued a hardware key on day 1.

## 8. Role-specific access

Access beyond the defaults is requested by the **hiring manager** through HelpPoint at least **5 working days before joining**, following the approval steps in IT-GDL-002: manager approval, then system owner approval, plus Security approval for Restricted data. Common examples:

| Role | Typical additional access |
|---|---|
| Sales and Marketing | LeadLoop CRM, marketing automation |
| Project managers | TrackWise project workspaces |
| Product managers | Product analytics, feedback tracker, TrackWise |
| Finance | Finance system, BuyRight approvals, bank portal (Restricted) |
| Engineering | Source code repositories, non-production cloud environments |
| HR | PeopleHub HR administration (Restricted) |

### 8.1 Access that requires training first

- **Production systems and customer data** are not granted until the joiner completes the Information Security Awareness and Data Protection modules (ONB-001).
- **Source code and engineering environments** additionally require the Secure Development module.
- **Payment systems** require Finance's payment-controls briefing.

## 9. The AI knowledge assistant for new joiners

The assistant is especially useful for new joiners, because it answers questions about policies and processes and shows the source. New joiners should know that:
- it searches only documents their role can access (IT-GDL-005);
- if their role in PeopleHub is wrong, the assistant will show the wrong set of documents, so they should report any mismatch to HR;
- answers should be checked against the cited source before acting on them.

## 10. Common day-1 problems and fixes

| Problem | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Cannot sign in with the temporary password | Password expired after 24 hours, or typed incorrectly | IT Service Desk issues a new temporary password by video call |
| MFA app not receiving prompts | Phone notifications blocked or wrong account registered | Re-register the authenticator with the Service Desk |
| Laptop asks for a recovery key | Encryption check after a hardware change | Service Desk provides the key after verifying identity |
| Role-specific system shows "no access" | Request not yet approved by the system owner | Manager follows up on the HelpPoint ticket |
| AI assistant shows unexpected documents | Incorrect department or job title in PeopleHub | HR corrects the record; role updates within 1 hour |
| Cannot connect to office Wi-Fi | Device certificate not yet installed | Connect via the guest network and VPN, then raise a P3 ticket |

Joiners should raise problems as soon as they occur rather than working around them; a workaround such as using a colleague's account is a breach of IT-GDL-002.

### 10.1 Returning employees

Employees re-joining Veltrix receive a new account and a newly imaged laptop; old accounts are never re-activated, because their permissions may no longer be appropriate. Historical mailbox data may be restored on request if it is still within the 3-year archive period set in IT-GDL-004.

## 11. Checks and quality measures

IT measures onboarding quality monthly:
- **Day-1 readiness:** percentage of joiners with laptop and default accounts working by 11:00 on day 1 (target 98%).
- **Week-1 access completion:** percentage of requested role-specific access granted by the end of week 1 (target 95%).
Missed targets are reviewed with HR Operations and hiring managers.

## 12. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| HR Operations | Enter accurate joiner details in PeopleHub at least 10 working days before joining |
| Hiring manager | Request role-specific access 5 working days before joining |
| IT Service Desk | Prepare laptop and accounts, enrol MFA, track readiness |
| System owners | Approve access requests promptly |
| Security team | Approve Restricted access; issue hardware keys |
| New joiner | Change temporary password, enrol MFA, complete required training, report access problems |

## 13. Exceptions

If HR confirms a joiner with less than 5 working days' notice, IT treats provisioning as a priority request but cannot guarantee day-1 readiness for role-specific access; default access is always prioritised. Access may never be granted by sharing another employee's account while waiting for approval.

## 14. Worked examples

**Example 1 - late confirmation.** HR confirms a joiner only 3 working days before the start date. IT creates default accounts the next day and prioritises the laptop, but LeadLoop access may follow during week 1.

**Example 2 - wrong department.** A new finance analyst is entered in PeopleHub with the department "Marketing" by mistake. On day 1 the AI assistant shows marketing documents instead of finance documents. The joiner reports it; HR corrects the record, and the role updates in the identity provider.

**Example 3 - production access.** A support engineer requests production database access on day 2. IT holds the request until the Information Security and Data Protection modules are completed.

**Example 4 - remote laptop.** A joiner in Chandigarh starts on Monday 2 March. The laptop must arrive by Friday 27 February.

## 15. Frequently asked questions

**Q: When will my accounts be created?**
A: Two working days before your joining date; you receive your temporary password on day 1.

**Q: Will my password be emailed to me?**
A: No. Credentials are never sent by email.

**Q: What access do I get by default?**
A: Email, TeamTalk, PeopleHub, ExpenseDesk, HelpPoint, the AI knowledge assistant and the password manager.

**Q: Why can't I access production systems yet?**
A: You must first complete the Information Security Awareness and Data Protection modules.

**Q: Who requests access to role-specific systems?**
A: Your hiring manager, at least 5 working days before you join.

**Q: What should I do if the AI assistant seems to show the wrong documents?**
A: Report it to HR; your department or job title in PeopleHub may be wrong.

## 16. Related documents and references

- ONB-001 New Employee Onboarding Programme; ONB-002 Manager's Onboarding Responsibilities Guide; ONB-005 Contractor and Intern Onboarding Procedure
- IT-GDL-001 Acceptable Use of IT Resources Guideline; IT-GDL-002 Identity, Password and Access Management Guideline; IT-GDL-003 Incident Reporting and Response; IT-GDL-004 Data Classification, Handling and Retention Guideline; IT-GDL-005 AI Assistant and Generative AI Usage Guideline
- Labelled contradiction example: CTR-005 (unofficial wiki page claiming laptops arrive within the first week)

## 17. Revision history

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | 2025-04-01 | Automated provisioning from PeopleHub |
| 2.1 | 2026-04-01 | Added AI assistant role guidance and readiness measures |

# Probation and Confirmation Policy

## 1. Purpose

Probation is a period at the start of employment in which the employee and the company confirm that the role is a good fit. It gives the employee time to learn the role with support, and gives the company a structured opportunity to assess performance and conduct before confirming employment. This policy sets the length of probation, how progress is reviewed, the possible outcomes, and the rights of the employee throughout.

## 2. Scope

The policy applies to all new permanent employees at every grade. It does not apply to:
- employees moving to a new role through internal transfer or promotion;
- former employees re-hired within 12 months of leaving, who return directly as confirmed employees;
- interns and contractors, who are covered by their engagement terms (ONB-005).
Fixed-term employees on contracts of less than 12 months do not serve probation; those on longer contracts serve probation as described here.

Part-time employees serve the same 6-month probation measured in calendar time, but managers should set goals that reflect their contracted hours, and the 30, 60 and 90-day check-ins may be combined where the role allows.

## 3. Length of probation

Probation lasts **6 months** from the date of joining. It may be **extended once, by up to 3 months**, under section 6.2. The total probation period can therefore never exceed 9 months.

If an employee is absent for more than 15 working days in total during probation (for example because of extended sick leave), the probation period is extended by the length of the absence beyond 15 working days, so that the employee has a fair amount of working time to demonstrate their abilities. Such an extension does not count as the single discretionary extension in section 6.2.

## 4. Support during probation

Every employee on probation receives:
- a structured onboarding programme with 30, 60 and 90-day check-ins (ONB-001);
- an onboarding buddy;
- clear goals recorded in PeopleHub;
- weekly one-to-ones with the manager;
- access to learning resources relevant to the role.

The performance review cycle described in HR-POL-003 does not apply until the employee is confirmed; probation reviews replace it.

## 5. Reviews during probation

| Review | Timing | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 30-day check-in | Around day 30 | Settling in and early goals |
| 60-day check-in | Around day 60 | Progress and support needed |
| 90-day review | Around day 90 | Written mid-probation review |
| Month-4 checkpoint | End of month 4 | Last point for documenting concerns that could affect confirmation |
| Confirmation review | **2 weeks before probation ends** | Manager's recommendation |

Any concern that may lead to an extension or ending of probation must be discussed with the employee and **documented in PeopleHub by the end of month 4**, with a support plan. Concerns raised for the first time at the confirmation review cannot by themselves justify ending employment, unless they concern serious misconduct that occurred after month 4.

## 6. Outcomes

### 6.1 Confirmation

When the employee has met the expectations of the role, the manager recommends confirmation in PeopleHub at the confirmation review. The HR business partner reviews the recommendation, and HR issues a **confirmation letter within 5 working days** of the decision. On confirmation:
- the notice period changes to the standard notice period for the grade (60 days for L1-L4 and 90 days for L5 and above);
- the employee becomes eligible for the one-time home office allowance under the Hybrid Work and Attendance Policy (HR-POL-002) and FIN-RMB-001;
- the limit on earned leave use during probation no longer applies (HR-POL-001).

### 6.2 Extension

Probation may be extended once, by up to 3 months, when the employee has made progress but has not yet fully met expectations, and the concerns were documented by month 4. The extension must be approved by the department head and HR business partner and communicated in writing **before the original probation end date**, with specific goals for the extension period.

### 6.3 Ending employment during probation

If the employee has not met expectations despite documented support, or after an unsuccessful extension, employment may end. The decision is approved by the department head and the HR business partner, and by the CHRO for grades L5 and above. Before a decision, the employee is told the concerns in writing and has **3 working days** to respond. Ending employment for gross misconduct follows HR-POL-005 at any stage.

### 6.4 No decision recorded

PeopleHub alerts the manager and HR business partner when the confirmation review is due. If no outcome has been recorded by the probation end date, HR escalates to the department head. **If no decision is recorded within 10 working days after the end date, the employee is deemed confirmed**, and HR issues the confirmation letter.

### 6.5 Communicating outcomes

All probation outcomes are communicated by the manager in a live conversation, with the HR business partner present for extensions and endings, before the written letter is issued. For an extension, the manager explains what has gone well, what still needs to improve, the specific goals for the extension period and the support that will be provided. For an ending, the employee is told the reasons, the notice arrangements and the exit steps, and is offered a meeting with HR to discuss final pay, leave encashment and the return of equipment. Outcomes are kept confidential; colleagues are told only that the person is leaving, unless the employee agrees to share more.

## 7. Notice during probation

During probation, either the employee or the company may end employment by giving **15 days' written notice**, or pay in lieu of notice. After confirmation the standard notice periods apply.

## 8. Leave and benefits during probation

Employees on probation receive full salary and benefits from day 1, including health insurance. Earned leave accrues from the first month, but **no more than 6 days of earned leave may be used during probation** without CHRO approval; casual and sick leave can be used normally (HR-POL-001).

## 9. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Employee | Engage with goals and feedback, ask for support, complete mandatory training |
| Manager | Set goals, hold check-ins, document concerns by month 4, recommend an outcome 2 weeks before the end |
| HR business partner | Review recommendations, ensure fairness and consistency, approve extensions and endings with the department head |
| Department head | Approve extensions and endings |
| CHRO | Approve endings for L5 and above; approve exceptions |
| HR Operations | Issue confirmation and extension letters, update PeopleHub |

## 10. Exceptions

The CHRO may shorten probation for senior hires with exceptional track records, or waive it for employees joining through an acquisition. Shortened probation must be stated in the offer letter. Any variation from this policy must be in writing.

## 11. Worked examples

**Example 1 - standard confirmation.** Anjali joins on 6 April. Her probation ends on 5 October. Her manager completes the confirmation review in the week of 21 September, two weeks before the end date, and HR issues her confirmation letter within 5 working days.

**Example 2 - extension.** Rohan's manager documented concerns about the quality of his reports at the end of month 3 and agreed a support plan. At the confirmation review, Rohan has improved but is not yet consistent. The department head and HR business partner approve a 2-month extension, communicated in writing before his original end date.

**Example 3 - undocumented concern.** In the final month of probation, a manager raises concerns about an employee's communication for the first time. Because nothing was documented by month 4, the employee cannot be refused confirmation on this basis alone; the manager should address it through normal feedback after confirmation.

**Example 4 - long sick leave.** Smita is absent for 25 working days during probation after surgery. Her probation is extended by 10 working days (the absence beyond 15 days). This is not counted as the single discretionary extension.

**Example 5 - no decision.** A manager is on leave and nobody records an outcome for Tarun by his end date. HR escalates; if no decision is recorded within 10 working days after the end date, Tarun is deemed confirmed.

## 12. Frequently asked questions

**Q: How long is probation?**
A: 6 months from the date of joining.

**Q: Can probation be extended?**
A: Yes, once, by up to 3 months, so the maximum is 9 months.

**Q: What is the notice period during probation?**
A: 15 days' written notice from either side.

**Q: When does my notice period become 60 or 90 days?**
A: On confirmation: 60 days for L1-L4 and 90 days for L5 and above.

**Q: How much earned leave can I use during probation?**
A: Up to 6 days without CHRO approval.

**Q: What happens if my manager forgets to complete my confirmation?**
A: HR escalates; if no decision is recorded within 10 working days after your end date, you are deemed confirmed.

**Q: Do I serve probation again if I am promoted?**
A: No. Probation does not apply to internal promotions or transfers.

## 13. Related documents and references

- ONB-001 New Employee Onboarding Programme; ONB-002 Manager's Onboarding Responsibilities Guide; ONB-005 Contractor and Intern Onboarding Procedure
- HR-POL-001 Leave and Holidays Policy; HR-POL-002 Hybrid Work and Attendance Policy; HR-POL-003 Performance Management Policy; HR-POL-005 Employee Conduct and Disciplinary Policy
- FIN-RMB-001 Expense Reimbursement Policy
- Labelled contradiction example: CTR-005 (unofficial wiki page stating a 3-month probation)

## 14. Revision history

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 2023-04-01 | Probation policy issued |
| 2.0 | 2026-04-01 | Added month-4 checkpoint, deemed confirmation rule and absence-based extension |

# Contractor and Intern Onboarding Procedure

## 1. Purpose

Contractors and interns make an important contribution at Veltrix, from specialist engineers on short projects to students gaining their first work experience. Because they are not permanent employees, their onboarding differs in contracts, access, duration and supervision. This procedure explains how managers engage and onboard them safely and fairly, and how their access is controlled and removed. It is restricted to managers and support functions because it covers commercial and access-control arrangements.

## 2. Scope and definitions

- **Contractor:** an individual who works for Veltrix through a vendor company or as an independent consultant under a services contract. Contractors are not on the Veltrix payroll.
- **Intern:** a student or recent graduate engaged directly by Veltrix for a fixed period of **2 to 6 months** for learning and project work, paid a stipend stated in the internship letter.
- **Sponsor:** the Veltrix manager responsible for the contractor or intern.

Fixed-term employees are not covered here; they follow the full onboarding programme (ONB-001).

## 3. Engaging a contractor

### 3.1 Commercial process

1. The sponsor confirms that the work cannot be done by internal staff within 4 weeks and that budget is available.
2. The sponsor raises a purchase request in **BuyRight**. The Procurement and Purchase Order Procedure (OPS-001) applies: a purchase order is required, and three quotes are needed above Rs 2,00,000 total contract value.
3. Approval follows the Delegation of Authority (OPS-002) based on the **total contract value**, not the monthly rate.
4. Where the contractor will access Confidential or Restricted data, the vendor must pass the **vendor security assessment** before the purchase order is issued.
5. The vendor contract includes confidentiality, data protection and intellectual property clauses; individual contractors also sign the Veltrix **non-disclosure agreement (NDA)** before receiving any access.

### 3.2 Contractor identity

Contractors receive a company account with the suffix *.ext* in the user name (for example *priya.sharma.ext*) and an **orange access badge**, so they can be identified easily. Contractors must not represent themselves to customers as Veltrix employees.

## 4. Engaging an intern

1. Interns are hired through the Recruitment and Selection Policy (HR-POL-004), usually through campus partnerships, with a simplified two-round process: one functional interview and one values interview.
2. The internship letter states the duration (2 to 6 months), stipend, working hours, base office, sponsor and mentor.
3. Each intern is assigned a **mentor** (who may also be the sponsor) and a defined project with clear learning goals.
4. Interns sign the NDA and the intellectual property assignment before starting.

## 5. Access for contractors and interns

### 5.1 Default access

| System | Contractors | Interns |
|---|---|---|
| Company email and TeamTalk | Yes | Yes |
| PeopleHub | No (vendor manages HR) | Yes (stipend, leave) |
| ExpenseDesk | No; expenses through vendor invoice | Yes, for approved business expenses |
| HelpPoint | Yes | Yes |
| AI knowledge assistant | Employee-level documents only | Employee-level documents only |

The AI knowledge assistant gives contractors and interns access only to documents available to the **employee** role, unless the sponsor requests a specific role-based extension through HelpPoint and the owning department approves it (IT-GDL-002).

### 5.2 Additional access

Additional access is requested by the sponsor in HelpPoint and follows the normal approvals. In addition:
- **Restricted data may not be accessed by contractors or interns without CISO approval.**
- Production systems require the same training as for employees (ONB-003).
- Interns do not receive privileged administrator access.

### 5.3 Account expiry

Contractor and intern accounts are created with an **expiry date no later than 6 months** after the start date, or the contract or internship end date if earlier. The sponsor receives a reminder 10 working days before expiry and must renew the account in HelpPoint if the engagement continues, confirming that the access is still needed. Accounts that are not renewed are disabled automatically on the expiry date.

## 6. Training and induction

Contractors and interns complete these modules **within 7 days of starting**, and before access to customer data:
- Code of Conduct and Ethics;
- Information Security Awareness;
- Data Protection and Privacy (CMP-003);
- POSH awareness.
Interns also attend the half-day company induction with new employees (ONB-001).

## 7. Supervision, leave and conduct

- Contractors' working hours and leave are agreed with their vendor and sponsor; Veltrix leave policies do not apply to them (HR-POL-001).
- Interns receive **1 day of paid leave per month** of internship, plus public holidays at their base office.
- Contractors and interns must follow the same standards of conduct as employees (HR-POL-005). Concerns about a contractor are raised by the sponsor with the vendor, and Veltrix may ask for the contractor to be replaced.

### 7.1 Intern projects and evaluation

Each intern project has a written brief agreed in the first week, listing the problem, the expected outputs, the tools and data the intern may use, and the review dates. Interns present their work to the team at the mid-point and at the end of the internship. The mentor completes a short evaluation covering technical skills, learning speed, communication and teamwork; this evaluation is used if the intern is considered for a permanent role. Interns must not be used as a substitute for permanent staff on routine operational work, and they do not handle customer escalations alone.

### 7.2 Intellectual property and data

Everything contractors and interns create in the course of their work for Veltrix, including code, documents, designs and data analyses, belongs to Veltrix under their contract or internship agreement. They may not reuse Veltrix material in other engagements, academic submissions or portfolios without written approval from the sponsor and, for anything containing Confidential data, from the information owner. Interns who need to submit a project report to their college must have the report reviewed by their sponsor so that no Confidential or Restricted information is included.

## 8. Ending the engagement

On the last day, the sponsor confirms in HelpPoint that the engagement has ended. IT disables accounts **within 24 hours** of the end date (the same day if the engagement ends early for conduct reasons), and the contractor or intern returns the laptop and badge. Interns receive an internship certificate and a feedback summary from their mentor. Work products and documents remain with Veltrix.

### 8.1 Interns joining full-time

Interns who perform well may be offered a permanent role. A conversion follows HR-POL-004 with a fast-track process (one final interview), and the intern then completes the full onboarding programme as a new employee, including probation (ONB-004).

## 9. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Sponsor | Justify the engagement, raise requests, supervise work, renew or end access on time |
| Mentor (interns) | Guide learning and project work; give regular feedback |
| Procurement | Run the contractor purchasing process (OPS-001) |
| HR Operations | Issue internship letters, manage intern records |
| IT Service Desk | Create time-limited accounts, disable them at expiry or end date |
| Security team | Run vendor assessments; approve Restricted access with the CISO |
| Finance | Pay vendor invoices against purchase orders; pay intern stipends |

## 10. Exceptions

Engagements of contractors longer than 12 months in total require a review by the department head and HR to confirm that the role should not be a permanent position. Any exception to account expiry or access rules must be approved by the CISO.

## 11. Worked examples

**Example 1 - contract value.** A project manager engages a contractor at Rs 1,50,000 per month for 4 months. The total contract value is Rs 6,00,000, so approval follows the Rs 5,00,001 to Rs 25,00,000 band in OPS-002 (Finance Controller), and three quotes are needed because the value is above Rs 2,00,000.

**Example 2 - account renewal.** A contractor's account expires on 31 August. The sponsor receives a reminder on 17 August and renews it after confirming the work continues.

**Example 3 - Restricted data.** A data contractor needs access to a dataset containing customer identity numbers (Restricted). Access requires CISO approval in addition to the normal approvals.

**Example 4 - intern leave.** An intern on a 3-month internship is entitled to 3 days of paid leave plus public holidays.

## 12. Frequently asked questions

**Q: How long can a contractor or intern account stay active?**
A: Up to 6 months from the start date, or the end date if earlier, unless renewed by the sponsor.

**Q: Can a contractor access Restricted data?**
A: Only with CISO approval.

**Q: What can contractors see in the AI knowledge assistant?**
A: Employee-level documents only, unless an extension is approved.

**Q: How long is an internship?**
A: Between 2 and 6 months.

**Q: How much leave do interns get?**
A: 1 day of paid leave per month of internship, plus public holidays.

**Q: Which approval level applies to a contractor engagement?**
A: The Delegation of Authority band for the total contract value.

**Q: When must contractors complete mandatory training?**
A: Within 7 days of starting and before accessing customer data.

## 13. Related documents and references

- ONB-001 New Employee Onboarding Programme; ONB-003 IT and Access Provisioning for New Joiners; ONB-004 Probation and Confirmation Policy
- HR-POL-001 Leave and Holidays Policy; HR-POL-004 Recruitment and Selection Policy; HR-POL-005 Employee Conduct and Disciplinary Policy
- IT-GDL-002 Identity, Password and Access Management Guideline; IT-GDL-004 Data Classification, Handling and Retention Guideline
- OPS-001 Procurement and Purchase Order Procedure; OPS-002 Delegation of Authority and Approval Workflow
- CMP-003 Data Protection and Privacy Policy

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 2024-07-01 | First contractor and intern procedure |
| 1.3 | 2026-04-01 | Account expiry set to 6 months; AI assistant access rules added |

source_reference: Fictional academic sample procedure for Veltrix Systems Pvt. Ltd.; refers in general terms to the MSMED Act, 2006 payment timelines
full_text:
# Procurement and Purchase Order Procedure

## 1. Purpose

Veltrix spends a significant share of its budget with external suppliers: cloud infrastructure, software licences, contractors, office services, events and equipment. This procedure makes sure that purchases are needed, competitively priced, properly approved, contracted on sound terms and paid correctly. It also protects the company against fraud, conflicts of interest and supplier risks. The procedure is restricted to managers and functions that buy on the company's behalf.

## 2. Scope

The procedure covers all purchases of goods and services from external suppliers, including contractors (ONB-005), software subscriptions and cloud services. It does not cover employee expense claims (FIN-RMB-001), corporate card purchases within card rules (FIN-RMB-005), payroll, or tax payments.

## 3. Key thresholds

| Rule | Threshold (total contract value, excluding taxes) |
|---|---|
| Purchase order (PO) required | **Above Rs 25,000** |
| Three competitive quotes required | **Above Rs 2,00,000** |
| Written contract reviewed by Legal | **Above Rs 5,00,000**, or any value if personal or Confidential data is involved |
| Formal request for proposal (RFP) with weighted scoring | **Above Rs 25,00,000** |
| Vendor security assessment | Any supplier that will store, process or access Confidential or Restricted data |

**Total contract value** means the full amount payable over the life of the contract, including all years of a multi-year subscription and all phases of a project. Splitting a requirement into smaller purchases to stay below a threshold is prohibited and is treated as serious misconduct.

## 4. The procurement process

### 4.1 Plan and justify

The requester checks that the purchase is in the approved budget and that no existing contract or internal resource already meets the need. For services, the requester writes a short scope of work describing deliverables, timelines and acceptance criteria.

### 4.2 Raise a purchase request

The requester raises a purchase request (PR) in **BuyRight**, attaching the scope, budget code, estimated value and preferred suppliers if known. The PR is approved by the requester's manager for business need before sourcing starts.

### 4.3 Source

| Value | Sourcing rule |
|---|---|
| Up to Rs 2,00,000 | One quote is enough; preferred suppliers should be used where available |
| Above Rs 2,00,000 up to Rs 25,00,000 | **At least three written quotes**, compared on price, quality, delivery and support |
| Above Rs 25,00,000 | **Formal RFP** issued by Procurement, with written evaluation criteria and weighted scoring by at least three evaluators |

Everyone involved in evaluating suppliers must declare any interest in a bidder before evaluation starts, and must step aside if a conflict exists (CMP-002).

#### 4.3.1 Single-source purchases

Where only one supplier can meet the need (for example renewal of a licence for a product already in use, or a proprietary integration), the requester completes a **single-source justification** in BuyRight. Single-source purchases above Rs 2,00,000 are approved by the Finance Controller in addition to the normal approvers.

### 4.4 Approve

Approval of the purchase follows the **Delegation of Authority and Approval Workflow (OPS-002)**, based on total contract value:

| Total contract value | Approver |
|---|---|
| Up to Rs 50,000 | Reporting manager |
| Rs 50,001 to Rs 5,00,000 | Department head |
| Rs 5,00,001 to Rs 25,00,000 | Finance Controller |
| Rs 25,00,001 to Rs 1,00,00,000 | CFO |
| Above Rs 1,00,00,000 | CEO, with Board approval |

BuyRight routes approvals automatically. Unbudgeted spend above Rs 5,00,000 also needs the Finance Controller's confirmation of funding.

### 4.5 Contract and purchase order

For purchases above Rs 5,00,000, or involving personal or Confidential data, Legal reviews the contract, including data protection, confidentiality, intellectual property, liability and termination clauses, and anti-bribery clauses for third parties who act on Veltrix's behalf (CMP-001). Procurement then issues the **purchase order** in BuyRight. **Suppliers must not start work before a PO is issued**, except in an emergency under section 6.

### 4.6 Contract renewals

Renewals are new commitments and need approval at the level matching the renewal's total value. BuyRight sends the requester a reminder **90 days before a contract's end date** so that there is time to review usage, compare alternatives and negotiate. Auto-renewing contracts must be cancelled or approved before the supplier's notice deadline; a renewal that happens automatically because nobody acted is still reported to the Finance Controller.

### 4.7 Supplier performance

For contracts above Rs 25,00,000, the business owner reviews the supplier's performance at least once a year against the agreed service levels, recording the result in BuyRight. Poor performance is raised with the supplier in writing, and repeated failures are considered before any renewal.

## 5. Supplier onboarding

Before a new supplier can receive a PO, Procurement completes onboarding:
- legal name, address and ownership details;
- PAN and GST registration, verified against government records;
- MSME registration status, if any;
- bank details, verified with a cancelled cheque or bank letter and a test transfer;
- vendor security assessment, where required;
- signed code of conduct for suppliers.

Ownership details are checked against employee conflict of interest declarations for contracts above Rs 25,00,000.

## 6. Emergency purchases

When an urgent purchase is needed to restore a critical service or prevent harm (for example replacing a failed network switch during a P1 incident), the department head may authorise the supplier to start before a PO is issued. A **retrospective PR and PO must be raised within 3 working days**, with the reason. Emergency purchases are reported monthly to the Finance Controller; repeated use for non-emergencies is escalated.

## 7. Receiving and payment

### 7.1 Goods and service receipt

The requester confirms in BuyRight that goods have been received or services delivered as agreed. Partial receipts are recorded for partial deliveries.

### 7.2 Three-way match

Accounts Payable matches the **PO, the receipt and the supplier's invoice**. **No PO, no pay:** invoices without a valid PO are returned to the supplier. Mismatches above **2% or Rs 10,000**, whichever is lower, are sent back to the requester to resolve.

### 7.3 Payment terms and runs

Standard payment terms are **45 days** from receipt of a correct invoice. Suppliers registered as micro or small enterprises are paid within 45 days as required by law, and never later. Payment runs take place every **Tuesday and Friday**.

### 7.4 Bank detail changes

A request from a supplier to change bank details is verified by a **call-back to a known contact number** from the supplier master record, never to a number in the request itself. Changes are approved by a second person in Finance before the next payment. This control protects against invoice fraud.

## 8. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Requester | Justify the need, raise the PR, write the scope, confirm receipt |
| Requester's manager | Approve business need |
| Procurement | Source suppliers, run RFPs, onboard suppliers, issue POs |
| Legal | Review contracts above Rs 5,00,000 or involving sensitive data |
| Security team | Run vendor security assessments |
| Accounts Payable | Three-way match, payments, bank detail verification |
| Approvers under OPS-002 | Approve purchases within their authority |
| Finance Controller | Own this procedure; approve single-source purchases above Rs 2,00,000 |

## 9. Exceptions

Exceptions to sourcing rules (for example accepting fewer than three quotes when only two suppliers respond) are approved by the Finance Controller and recorded in BuyRight. Exceptions to approval limits are not permitted.

## 10. Worked examples

**Example 1 - laptop accessories.** A team needs monitors worth Rs 1,40,000. A PO is required (above Rs 25,000), one quote is enough (below Rs 2,00,000), and the department head approves (Rs 50,001 to Rs 5,00,000).

**Example 2 - multi-year subscription.** A software tool costs Rs 4,00,000 per year on a 3-year contract. The total contract value is Rs 12,00,000, so three quotes are needed, Legal reviews the contract, and the Finance Controller approves.

**Example 3 - split purchase.** A manager raises two POs of Rs 1,90,000 each for the same training programme to avoid the three-quote rule. This is prohibited splitting; the total of Rs 3,80,000 requires three quotes.

**Example 4 - emergency.** A storage controller fails at 23:00 during a P1 incident. The department head authorises a replacement immediately, and a retrospective PO is raised within 3 working days.

**Example 5 - bank change.** An email from a supplier asks for payments to a new bank account. Accounts Payable calls the supplier's known contact from the master record, discovers the email is fraudulent, and reports it as a security incident.

## 11. Frequently asked questions

**Q: When is a purchase order required?**
A: For any purchase above Rs 25,000.

**Q: When do I need three quotes?**
A: When the total contract value is above Rs 2,00,000.

**Q: When is a formal RFP required?**
A: Above Rs 25,00,000.

**Q: Who approves a Rs 30,00,000 contract?**
A: The CFO (Rs 25,00,001 to Rs 1,00,00,000).

**Q: Can a supplier start work before the PO?**
A: Only in an emergency authorised by the department head, with a retrospective PO within 3 working days.

**Q: What are the standard payment terms?**
A: 45 days from receipt of a correct invoice.

**Q: How are bank detail changes verified?**
A: By a call-back to a known contact number from the supplier master record.

## 12. Related documents and references

- OPS-002 Delegation of Authority and Approval Workflow
- CMP-001 Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy; CMP-002 Conflict of Interest and Gifts Policy; CMP-003 Data Protection and Privacy Policy
- FIN-RMB-001 Expense Reimbursement Policy; FIN-RMB-005 Corporate Card, Travel Advance and Petty Cash Policy
- ONB-005 Contractor and Intern Onboarding Procedure
- IT-GDL-004 Data Classification, Handling and Retention Guideline
- Labelled contradiction example: CTR-004 (draft procurement note with different thresholds)

## 13. Revision history

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 3.0 | 2025-04-01 | Thresholds aligned with revised Delegation of Authority |
| 3.1 | 2026-04-01 | Added single-source justification and emergency purchase rule |

title: Delegation of Authority and Approval Workflow
applies_to: All managers, department heads and executives who approve spend, contracts, hiring, pricing or policy decisions

full_text:
# Delegation of Authority and Approval Workflow

## 1. Purpose

The Board of Directors is ultimately responsible for Veltrix's decisions, but it delegates day-to-day authority to management so that the company can operate efficiently. This Delegation of Authority (DoA) sets out **who can approve what, and up to what limit**, for spend, contracts, hiring, pricing, write-offs and policies. It also defines the principles that make approvals valid, how authority can be delegated temporarily, and how approval workflows operate in company systems. It is the single reference for approval limits; other policies refer to it rather than repeating limits.

## 2. Scope

The DoA applies to every decision that commits Veltrix financially or legally, or changes how the company operates. It applies in all offices and to all systems in which approvals are recorded, including BuyRight, ExpenseDesk, PeopleHub and the contract management tool.

## 3. Approval principles

1. **Approve only within your limit.** Anything above your limit must go to the next level.
2. **Total value.** Limits apply to the total value of a commitment over its full life (for example all years of a subscription), not to an annual or monthly amount.
3. **No self-approval.** Nobody may approve their own expense, purchase, travel or pay change, or one from which they personally benefit.
4. **Separation of duties.** The person who requests a purchase may not be the only approver, and the person who approves a payment may not also create the supplier record.
5. **Approve in the system.** Approvals are valid only when recorded in the relevant system. Email or verbal approvals are valid only in a genuine emergency and must be recorded in the system within **3 working days**.
6. **Budget is not approval.** Having budget for something does not mean it is approved; the approval steps still apply.
7. **No splitting.** Breaking a commitment into smaller parts to stay within a lower limit is prohibited.
8. **AI support only.** The internal AI knowledge assistant can explain approval rules but cannot approve anything (IT-GDL-005).

## 4. Spend approval limits

These limits apply to purchases, contracts with suppliers, expense claims, travel costs and other spend commitments.

| Total value | Approver |
|---|---|
| **Up to Rs 50,000** | Reporting manager |
| **Rs 50,001 to Rs 5,00,000** | Department head |
| **Rs 5,00,001 to Rs 25,00,000** | Finance Controller |
| **Rs 25,00,001 to Rs 1,00,00,000** | CFO |
| **Above Rs 1,00,00,000** | CEO, with Board approval |

Additional rules:
- **Unbudgeted spend above Rs 5,00,000** also needs the Finance Controller's confirmation of funding, whatever the approver.
- Capital expenditure above **Rs 10,00,000** needs a business case with a net present value calculation at a **12% hurdle rate**, reviewed by Finance before approval.
- Procurement rules (quotes, RFPs, contracts) are in OPS-001.

## 5. Contract signing authority

| Contract value | Who may sign |
|---|---|
| Up to Rs 25,00,000 | Department head together with the Finance Controller |
| Rs 25,00,001 to Rs 1,00,00,000 | CFO |
| Above Rs 1,00,00,000 | CEO, after Board approval |
| Customer contracts on standard terms | VP Sales, any value, within approved pricing |
| Any contract with non-standard liability, indemnity or data protection terms | As above, plus Head of Legal and Compliance review |
| Non-disclosure agreements on the standard template | Any department head |

Nobody else may sign contracts on behalf of Veltrix. Contracts signed without authority may not bind the company and are a disciplinary matter.

## 6. People decisions

| Decision | Approver |
|---|---|
| Budgeted backfill position | Department head |
| Budgeted new position | Department head and HR business partner |
| Unbudgeted position within department budget | Department head and CHRO |
| Unbudgeted position exceeding department budget | CHRO and CFO |
| Offer up to band midpoint | Hiring manager and HR business partner |
| Offer above midpoint up to band maximum | CHRO |
| Offer above band maximum, or joining bonus above Rs 2,00,000 | CHRO and CFO |
| Promotion | Department head and HR business partner |
| Termination for misconduct or performance | CHRO |
| Relocation support above the standard package | CHRO (and CFO where the excess is above Rs 1,00,000) |

Details are in HR-POL-004, HR-POL-005 and FIN-RMB-003.

## 7. Pricing and revenue decisions

| Discount off list price on a customer deal | Approver |
|---|---|
| Up to 10% | Sales Manager |
| 10.1% to 20% | VP Sales |
| 20.1% to 30% | CFO |
| Above 30% | CEO |

Changes to list prices require approval by the VP Product, CFO and CEO. Write-off of customer receivables up to Rs 1,00,000 is approved by the Finance Controller, up to Rs 10,00,000 by the CFO, and above that by the CEO.

## 8. Other decisions

| Decision | Approver |
|---|---|
| Domestic business travel | Reporting manager (FIN-RMB-002) |
| International business travel | Department head |
| Business class travel | CFO |
| Charitable donations | CFO and CEO (CMP-001) |
| Access to Restricted data | Manager, system owner and Security (IT-GDL-002) |
| New or changed company policy | As set out in OPS-005 |
| Security exceptions | CISO |

### 8.1 Combining limits

Some decisions involve more than one table. For example, hiring a contractor through a vendor is both a people decision and a purchase: the business need is approved by the department head, and the purchase is approved at the spend level for the total contract value. Where two approvals apply, both are required, and the more senior approver signs last. A decision with both spend and pricing elements, such as a customer deal that includes a discount and a third-party cost, needs the discount approver and the spend approver.

## 9. Temporary delegation

An approver who is on leave or unavailable may delegate their authority **in writing in the relevant system** (BuyRight, ExpenseDesk or PeopleHub) to a person at the **same level or above** for a maximum of **30 days**. Delegation to a more junior person is not permitted. The delegate's approvals are recorded under their own name with a note of the delegation. Delegations end automatically on the end date.

## 10. Approval workflow in systems

1. The requester submits the item in the system with the value, cost centre and supporting documents.
2. The system determines the required approvers from the value and type, using this DoA.
3. Each approver reviews and approves or rejects within **3 working days**; overdue approvals are escalated automatically to the approver's manager.
4. Rejected items return to the requester with a reason.
5. The final approval is recorded with a time stamp and is available for audit.

Finance reviews the system configuration whenever this DoA changes, so that systems and policy always match.

## 11. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Approvers | Approve only within their authority, check business need and budget, record approvals in systems |
| Requesters | Provide accurate values and documents; never split commitments |
| Finance | Maintain this DoA, configure systems, audit approvals |
| Internal Audit | Test compliance with the DoA annually |
| CFO | Own this policy and propose changes to the Board |
| Board of Directors | Approve the DoA and changes to it |

## 12. Exceptions

The DoA cannot be overridden by any individual. In a genuine emergency, the CEO may approve a commitment above their limit only to protect people, assets or critical services, and must report it to the Board within 7 days.

## 13. Worked examples

**Example 1 - software purchase.** A Rs 3,00,000 annual subscription for one year: department head approval. The same subscription for three years (Rs 9,00,000 total): Finance Controller approval.

**Example 2 - discount.** A sales manager negotiates a 25% discount with a customer. The CFO must approve (20.1% to 30%).

**Example 3 - delegation.** The Finance Controller goes on leave for two weeks and delegates approval authority in BuyRight to the CFO, who is at a higher level. Delegation to a finance manager would not be allowed.

**Example 4 - unbudgeted spend.** Marketing wants an unbudgeted Rs 8,00,000 event sponsorship. The Finance Controller approves (Rs 5,00,001 to Rs 25,00,000) and must also confirm funding because it is unbudgeted.

**Example 5 - emergency email approval.** During a weekend outage, the department head approves an emergency hardware purchase by email. The approval must be recorded in BuyRight within 3 working days.

## 14. Frequently asked questions

**Q: Who approves spend of Rs 4,00,000?**
A: The department head (Rs 50,001 to Rs 5,00,000).

**Q: Who approves spend of Rs 60,00,000?**
A: The CFO (Rs 25,00,001 to Rs 1,00,00,000).

**Q: Does the limit apply to the annual or total value?**
A: To the total value over the full life of the commitment.

**Q: Can I approve my own expense claim?**
A: No. Self-approval is never allowed.

**Q: Can I delegate my approvals while on leave?**
A: Yes, in writing in the system, to someone at the same level or above, for up to 30 days.

**Q: Who approves a 15% customer discount?**
A: The VP Sales.

**Q: Is an email approval valid?**
A: Only in a genuine emergency, and it must be recorded in the system within 3 working days.

**Q: Can the AI assistant approve a request?**
A: No. It can explain the rules but cannot approve anything.

## 15. Related documents and references

- OPS-001 Procurement and Purchase Order Procedure; OPS-005 Document Control and Policy Management Procedure
- FIN-RMB-001 Expense Reimbursement Policy; FIN-RMB-002 Business Travel Policy; FIN-RMB-003 Relocation and Joining Expense Policy; FIN-RMB-005 Corporate Card, Travel Advance and Petty Cash Policy
- HR-POL-004 Recruitment and Selection Policy; HR-POL-005 Employee Conduct and Disciplinary Policy
- IT-GDL-002 Identity, Password and Access Management Guideline; IT-GDL-005 AI Assistant and Generative AI Usage Guideline
- CMP-001 Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy

## 16. Revision history

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 4.0 | 2025-04-01 | Limits revised; CEO and Board threshold set at Rs 1 crore |
| 4.1 | 2026-04-01 | Added contract signing authority, write-off limits and AI assistant rule |

full_text:
# Business Continuity and Crisis Management Procedure

## 1. Purpose

Floods, power failures, cyber-attacks, pandemics and the loss of a key supplier can all disrupt Veltrix's ability to serve customers and support employees. This procedure explains how the company prepares for such events, how it decides that a situation is a crisis, who leads the response, how critical activities are kept running or restored within agreed times, and how the company communicates with employees, customers and the public. It is restricted to the functions that plan and lead the response; employee-facing emergency instructions are in OPS-004.

## 2. Scope

The procedure covers all offices, remote work arrangements, company systems and the Veltrix products that customers depend on. It covers events affecting people (illness, injury, safety threats), places (office unavailable), technology (major outage or cyber-attack) and suppliers (failure of a critical vendor).

## 3. Definitions

- **Business continuity:** the ability to continue delivering critical activities at an acceptable level during a disruption.
- **Crisis:** a situation that threatens the safety of people, the continuity of critical activities, or the company's reputation, and requires coordinated leadership beyond normal management.
- **Business impact analysis (BIA):** a structured assessment of how quickly each activity must be restored and what it depends on.
- **Recovery time objective (RTO):** the maximum acceptable time to restore an activity or system.
- **Recovery point objective (RPO):** the maximum acceptable loss of data, measured in time.

## 4. Governance

### 4.1 Crisis Management Team

The **Crisis Management Team (CMT)** leads the company's response to any declared crisis. Members:
- **CEO** (chair);
- CFO;
- CHRO;
- CIO;
- CISO;
- CMO (communications);
- Head of Operations (coordinator).
Each member has a named deputy. The Head of Legal and Compliance joins when legal or regulatory issues arise.

### 4.2 Business continuity coordinators

Each department names a business continuity coordinator who keeps the department's continuity plan current, participates in exercises and acts as the contact point during a disruption.

## 5. Business impact analysis and critical activities

The BIA is **reviewed every year** by the Head of Operations with each department. The current critical activities and recovery objectives are:

| Critical activity | RTO | RPO | Main dependencies |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer production platforms (Veltrix Insight, Flow, Connect) | **8 hours** | **4 hours** | Cloud hosting, on-call engineering |
| Customer support | **4 hours** | Not applicable | Support tool, telephony, support staff |
| Identity, email and TeamTalk | 8 hours | 4 hours | Identity provider, cloud services |
| Payroll | **48 hours**, and salaries must be paid by the last working day of the month | 1 day | Payroll system, bank portal, Payroll team |
| Supplier payments | 5 working days | 1 day | Finance system, bank portal |
| Month-end close | Completed by working day 5, with up to 3 days' delay acceptable in a declared crisis | 1 day | Finance system, Finance team |

The IT recovery objectives match the Backup and Disaster Recovery standard applied by IT (RPO 4 hours, RTO 8 hours) and the backup retention in IT-GDL-004.

## 6. Preparation

- Each department maintains a continuity plan listing critical activities, minimum staff, alternative ways of working, key contacts and suppliers.
- Critical roles have at least one trained back-up person.
- Work can move to remote working or another office: all employees have laptops and VPN access, and the hybrid model (HR-POL-002) means remote working is routine.
- Critical suppliers (cloud hosting, payroll provider, bank, telephony) are reviewed annually for their own continuity arrangements.
- Contact details for all employees are kept up to date in PeopleHub; the emergency notification system draws on these records.

## 7. Detecting and declaring a crisis

### 7.1 Escalation

Any manager who becomes aware of a serious event (for example an office fire, a P1 incident lasting more than 4 hours, a SEV-1 security incident, a natural disaster affecting an office city, or a death or serious injury at work) informs the Head of Operations immediately. IT incidents follow IT-GDL-003 and are escalated to the CMT when they meet these criteria.

### 7.2 Declaration

The Head of Operations convenes the CMT, or its available members, **within 1 hour**. The CEO, or the CFO in the CEO's absence, decides whether to **declare a crisis**. Once declared, the CMT:
1. confirms the facts and the immediate risks to people;
2. sets priorities: people first, then customers, then other operations;
3. assigns workstreams (people and safety, technology, customers, communications, finance);
4. agrees the next meeting time, normally every 2 to 4 hours during the acute phase.

## 8. Protecting people

- **Emergency notification:** employees affected by an event receive a message through TeamTalk and SMS **within 30 minutes** of the CMT deciding it is needed, with clear instructions.
- **Safety check-in:** employees in an affected location confirm they are safe through the notification system; HR follows up with anyone who has not responded **within 2 hours**.
- **Travellers:** the Travel Desk uses the travel register (FIN-RMB-002) to identify and contact employees travelling in affected areas.
- **Support:** HR arranges medical help, counselling through the employee assistance programme, and flexible leave for affected employees.

## 9. Keeping critical activities running

Departments activate their continuity plans for the affected activities. Typical measures include moving work to remote working or to another office, switching support calls to another location, restoring systems from backups in a different cloud region, and using back-up suppliers. IT technical recovery follows IT-GDL-003 and the disaster recovery runbooks. Finance makes sure that payroll and essential supplier payments continue, using manual bank-portal payments if needed, approved under the Delegation of Authority.

## 10. Communication

| Audience | Responsibility | Channel |
|---|---|---|
| Employees | CHRO with Internal Communications | TeamTalk, email, SMS, manager briefings |
| Customers | Customer Success with the CMO | Status page, account managers, email |
| Media and public | **Only the CEO, the CMO or a named spokesperson** | Approved statements |
| Regulators and authorities | Head of Legal and Compliance, CISO for CERT-In matters | As required |

All external statements are approved by the CMT. Employees must not comment publicly or on social media about a crisis. Where personal data is affected, the Data Protection Officer leads notification under CMP-003.

## 11. Recovery and review

The CMT stands down when critical activities are restored and the risk to people has passed. A **post-crisis review is completed within 15 working days**, covering what happened, how the response worked, and improvements. Improvements are tracked to completion by the Head of Operations.

## 12. Testing and exercises

- Each department's continuity plan is **tested at least once a year**, through a desk-top exercise or a live test.
- The CMT runs **one crisis simulation every year**, rotating scenarios (for example ransomware, office closure, pandemic, cloud region outage).
- IT runs disaster recovery tests **twice a year**.
- Evacuation drills are run under OPS-004.
Results and improvement actions are reported to the CEO.

## 13. Roles and responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| CEO | Chair the CMT; declare and stand down crises |
| Head of Operations | Maintain this procedure and the BIA; coordinate the CMT; run exercises |
| CHRO | People and safety workstream; employee communications |
| CIO and CISO | Technology recovery and security response |
| CFO | Financial continuity; emergency spend under the DoA |
| CMO | External and customer communications |
| Department coordinators | Maintain and test department plans |

## 14. Exceptions

During a declared crisis, the CMT may temporarily vary normal procedures, including approval workflows, where needed to protect people or critical services. Every variation is recorded in the crisis log and reviewed in the post-crisis review. Spend approvals above normal limits follow the emergency rule in the Delegation of Authority.

## 15. Worked examples

**Example 1 - flooding in Bengaluru.** Heavy rain closes roads around the Bengaluru office. The CMT declares a crisis for the location, notifies Bengaluru employees within 30 minutes to work from home, and HR completes safety check-ins within 2 hours.

**Example 2 - cloud region outage.** A cloud provider region hosting Veltrix Insight fails. IT restores the service in a secondary region within the 8-hour RTO, with data loss no greater than the 4-hour RPO. Customer Success updates the status page.

**Example 3 - payroll at risk.** A ransomware attack on 27 March disables the payroll system. Finance uses the bank portal and the last approved payroll file, adjusted manually, so that salaries are paid by 31 March.

**Example 4 - media enquiry.** A journalist contacts an engineer about an outage. The engineer politely declines and passes the request to the CMO.

## 16. Frequently asked questions

**Q: Who chairs the Crisis Management Team?**
A: The CEO; the CFO decides on declaration in the CEO's absence.

**Q: How quickly must the CMT meet after a serious event?**
A: Within 1 hour of the Head of Operations being informed.

**Q: How quickly are employees notified?**
A: Within 30 minutes of the CMT deciding a notification is needed.

**Q: What is the RTO for customer production platforms?**
A: 8 hours, with an RPO of 4 hours.

**Q: How often is the business impact analysis reviewed?**
A: Every year.

**Q: Who may speak to the media during a crisis?**
A: Only the CEO, the CMO or a named spokesperson.

**Q: When is the post-crisis review completed?**
A: Within 15 working days of standing down.

## 17. Related documents and references

- OPS-004 Facilities, Office Access and Workplace Safety Procedure
- IT-GDL-003 Information Security Incident Reporting and Response Guideline; IT-GDL-004 Data Classification, Handling and Retention Guideline
- FIN-RMB-002 Business Travel Policy; HR-POL-002 Hybrid Work and Attendance Policy
- CMP-003 Data Protection and Privacy Policy
- OPS-002 Delegation of Authority and Approval Workflow
- External: ISO 22301 (general concepts)

## 18. Revision history

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 2023-10-01 | First continuity procedure |
| 2.0 | 2026-04-01 | Recovery objectives aligned with IT standards; safety check-in and payroll continuity added |
